picks.headline: Staff predictions for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt: Can the Hokies start 5-0?
picks.blurb: BLACKSBURG, Va. — Virginia Tech football takes on Pitt tomorrow night in its fifth contest of the 2026 season. Ahead of the Friday evening clash against the Panthers, three members of our staff offered their thoughts on what could unfold tomorrow: JACKSON CAUDELL: This is the biggest Virginia Tech game in years. If they win, they will be 5-0 and have a win against one of the teams expected to compete for a spot in the ACC Championship game, giving them a huge tiebreaker. You could argue that the winner of this game is going to be in the best position to make it to Charlotte and likely face Miami . I expect this to be a close game, but the home-field advantage and Virginia Tech's defense are going to be the difference. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Pitt 20 JAMES DUNCAN: Nobody has scored on Pitt in the first or third quarter this season. The Panthers allow 8.5 points per game, fewest in the ACC. Against a Virginia Tech line missing left tackle Justin Terry, I don't see the Hokies hanging 40. Expect quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer to live on quick throws to tight end Luke Reynolds. But Pitt has been flagged 37 times for 359 yards, all at home. Now its first road trip is Lane Stadium on a Friday night. If pre-snap penalties have been an issue at home, who knows what it will be in front of 65,000 people screaming at the top of their lungs when trying to hear a snap count. I still expect this game to come down to the final snap. In fact, I’m predicting a walk-off field goal from John Love to give James Franklin his signature moment in his first season at Virginia Tech. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Pitt 21 THOMAS HUGHES: Virginia Tech has an opportunity to turn a promising start into a true renaissance Friday night. Pitt presents a challenge on defense, and the Hokies will need to help Ethan Grunkemeyer avoid spending the evening under pressure. Quick throws to Luke Reynolds and a productive rushing attack should be central to that effort, and they should be more available than in last Saturday's rainy affair in Chestnut Hill. Still, I trust Virginia Tech to find enough offense to keep this game within reach throughout. The bigger question is whether the Hokies can force Pitt into the mistakes that become increasingly costly in a close conference matchup. Lane Stadium should have something to say about that, particularly if the Panthers struggle with penalties. I expect a competitive game that remains undecided into the fourth quarter, but that Virginia Tech’s defense delivers the final stop to keep James Franklin’s team unbeaten and firmly in the ACC conversation. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect James Duncan Fri, October 2, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Pitt hasn't allowed a point in the first or third quarter this season. Pitt also hasn't left Pittsburgh. That changes today at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN, when the Panthers (4-0, 1-0 ACC) walk into a sold-out Lane Stadium to face a Virginia Tech team (4-0, 1-0 ACC) chasing its first 5-0 start since 2005. The winner moves into a three-way tie for first place in the ACC. "It'll be one of the louder games we play," Pitt head coach Pat Narduzzi said this week. Here are three bold predictions for the game. 1. Jeffrey Overton Jr. runs for 100 yards on the nation's No. 4 run defense Pitt has allowed 213 rushing yards in four games. Overton ran for 209 yards last Saturday at Boston College, including the 76-yard touchdown that put Virginia Tech ahead for good in a 21-14 win. That earned him ACC Running Back of the Week. The sophomore missed the first eight games of last season with an injury and finished 2025 with 25 carries. He already has 60 this fall, for 409 yards and four rushing touchdowns at 6.8 yards per carry. He'll run Friday without left tackle Justin Terry, who is out. That's a real problem against a defense allowing 53.3 rushing yards per game. 2. Mason Heintschel leaves Blacksburg without a touchdown pass Pitt's sophomore quarterback has thrown 13 touchdown passes, second in the ACC. Seven came against Miami (Ohio). Six came against Bucknell. Against UCF and Syracuse, he went 28 of 52 for 335 yards with no touchdowns and an interception. The Panthers got past Syracuse by running for 245 yards, and true freshman running back Damon Ferguson Jr. leads the team with 239 yards for the season. Virginia Tech has to take that away first. Then comes the hard part for Heintschel. This is his first road start of the season, against a defense that leads the nation with 45 tackles for loss and 17 sacks. The risk sits behind Virginia Tech's front. Maryland threw for 359 yards and three touchdowns on the Hokies two weeks ago, and Virginia Tech has one interception in four games. Defensive coordinator Brent Pry's group doesn't have to be perfect. It has to make Heintschel uncomfortable, and no defense in the country has lived in the backfield more. 3. John Love hits a walk-off field goal, and Virginia Tech is ranked by Sunday John Love has scored 313 points in a Virginia Tech uniform. The next three decide Friday night. "This is going to be a battle," Virginia Tech head coach James Franklin said Monday. Franklin would know. He faced Narduzzi four times from 2016-19 when he was at Penn State. Pitt leads the ACC at 8.5 points allowed per game and hasn't given up more than 14 to anyone. I have Virginia Tech get past that number, but not by much. The Panthers stay in it on the ground, the way they did against Syracuse. That leaves it to Love. The fifth-year kicker is fourth on Virginia Tech's all-time scoring list, has a career-long of 60 yards, and went 2 for 2 at Boston College. He gets one more with the clock running out. Virginia Tech wins 24-21. The Hokies have 86 points in the AP poll, fifth among teams outside the Top 25, and haven't been ranked since 2021.With a win on Friday night, it will be hard to leave them out for another week. picks.blurb: Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus NFL Power Rankings Rays top sloppy Yankees Week 5 Waiver Wire Falcons run over Saints White Sox up 2-0 in ALDS Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt Virginia Tech Athletics Thomas Hughes Fri, October 2, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads BLACKSBURG, Va. - For the first time in 20 days, Virginia Tech football hosts a game at Lane Stadium - this one against Pitt with a 5-0 start hanging in the balance. Both the Hokies (4-0, 1-0 ACC) and Panthers (4-0, 1-0 ACC) enter Friday night's contest with unblemished marks, making the matchup one of four games nationally this week between undefeated FBS teams. For Virginia Tech, a victory would secure its first 5-0 start since 2005 and continue a remarkable turnaround in James Franklin's first season at the helm. Virginia Tech's perfect record hasn't come without adversity. After opening the season with commanding victories over VMI (73-3) and Old Dominion (44-21), the Hokies survived consecutive road tests against Maryland and Boston College . Tech defeated the Terrapins 35-26 before escaping a rain-soaked Chestnut Hill with a 21-14 victory. The latter required Virginia Tech to overcome a 14-6 fourth-quarter deficit. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led an 80-yard touchdown drive that ended with a 14-yard score to Marlion Jackson, and Jeffrey Overton Jr. broke free for a 76-yard touchdown less than three minutes later to put the Hokies ahead for good. Overton's emergence has added another dimension to an offense that relied heavily on Grunkemeyer through the first three weeks. The sophomore enters Friday with 409 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 60 carries, averaging 6.8 yards per attempt. He erupted for a career-high 209 yards on 25 carries against Boston College, earning ACC Running Back of the Week honors. Finding similar success against Pitt, though, will be difficult. The Panthers enter Blacksburg allowing just 53.3 rushing yards per game and 8.5 points per contest. Pitt's defense has surrendered just 34 points through four games, following a 59-14 win over Miami (Ohio) with victories of 12-7 over UCF, 27-13 over Syracuse and 59-0 over Bucknell. That creates perhaps the game's most important matchup. Virginia Tech has found a potential difference-maker in Overton, but Pitt possesses one of the stingiest rushing defenses in the country. If the Panthers can prevent Overton from consistently reaching the second level, more responsibility will fall back onto Grunkemeyer. The Penn State transfer has largely handled that responsibility well. Grunkemeyer has completed 101 of 136 passes for 1,012 yards, eight touchdowns and no interceptions through four games. Boston College limited him to 147 passing yards, but the weather played a significant factor. Pitt quarterback Mason Heintschel has completed 88 of 130 passes for 1,191 yards, 13 touchdowns and just one interception. His season began with a historic seven-touchdown performance against Miami (Ohio), and he threw for 403 yards and six touchdowns in last week's demolition of Bucknell. Heintschel became the first ACC quarterback to record multiple six-touchdown passing games in the same season. That should provide Virginia Tech's pass rush with its biggest challenge yet. The Hokies have consistently disrupted opposing backfields, entering Friday averaging 4.25 sacks and 11.3 tackles for loss per game. Cortez Harris has led that charge with five sacks, including two in the victory over Boston College. Getting to Heintschel could be critical. Pitt averages 347.3 passing yards and 39.3 points per game, and its passing attack isn't dependent on a single target. Thirteen different Panthers caught a pass against Bucknell, while five players hauled in touchdowns. Censere Lee led the scoring barrage with three touchdown receptions. Friday also represents something Pitt hasn't experienced this season: a road game. The Panthers played each of their first four contests at Acrisure Stadium and now head into a sold-out Lane Stadium for a primetime matchup. Pitt is 3-8 all-time in Blacksburg, although the Panthers have won three of the last four overall meetings between the programs. Virginia Tech won the most recent matchup, 38-21, in 2023. Virginia Tech has answered four different tests through four weeks. Pitt presents another, and perhaps the most complete one yet. One undefeated record will disappear Friday night. Which one do I think will? Virginia Tech's defense should give Pitt its toughest test yet, while Lane Stadium could make the Panthers' first road game uncomfortable. The Hokies may not completely contain Heintschel, but Overton and Grunkemeyer should generate enough offense late to preserve the unbeaten start in a tightly contested ACC matchup. Tech is a narrow homefield favorite, but the media and commentariat don’t agree. It’s looking like a season where the upcoming game is the most important game of the season. If you had to pick a really obvious one out of the stack, the Pitt game runs right to the top of the flagpole. Let’s look at some team news, a few updates here and there, and then get to the predictions. It’s not Homecoming, but It is Stripe Lane Night The program has fan gimmicks for most games this season, and it’s a night where certain sections wear orange, and others wear maroon. Sometimes it works out, and sometimes it sort of looks like more than half the people didn’t care or didn’t know. Just a Reminder that the Team in Maroon Earned Its Way Last Saturday in a New England coastal Nor’easter, the Hokies earned their respect the hard way, by fighting BC and the weather to catch, pass, and then burn out the clock before they had a chance to respond. Jeffrey Overton, Jr. Gets Some Kudos He gets named ACC Running Back of the Week for his powerful performance in the rain and wind of Alumni Stadium. PFF picks out Overton but also adds Quentin Reddish and Jaquez White for their National Team of the Week notice. Catch Up with Coach Franklin’s Weekly Presser This is nearly a 51-minute watch so go grab a coffee. Lots of good information in this one. Predictions Time Huge game for the Hokies. This game means a lot for several reasons. A chance to go 5-0, a chance to go 2-0 in the ACC, a chance to re-establish Lane Stadium as a place that visiting teams dread coming to play. Pitt is a tough challenge. Under Pat Narduzzi, the Panthers always play a tough brand of football. They generally play solid defense and rely on the running game. They now have a quarterback who can air it out. Pitt’s strengths and Virginia Tech’s potential weaknesses match up well for the Panthers. The Hokies have allowed some big plays through the air this year, so Pitt will test that. I have concerns about Pitt’s run defense. The Hokies have had some issues at times this year and are dealing with multiple injuries along the offensive line. That’s something to watch. I do think the Hokies will make some plays in the running game. More Jeffrey Overton, please. Luke Reynolds had a down game last week, due to the weather more than anything, but I expect a big bounce-back this week. Reynolds catches another touchdown and quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer is the better quarterback on the field again this week. It’s close, but the Hokies win. Virginia Tech 27, Pitt 21 Tough games require some tough thinking. This one is essentially a toss-up, and regardless of these two teams’ records they always seem to be a fist fight street brawl. This season neither team is ranked, but neither is showing up at Lane Stadium with a loss on their record. Tech is rallying up behind a completely revamped and very different offense than we have seen since the Michael Brewer days at the end of the Beamer Era. This Tech team has an actual quarterback, uses its tight ends and gets downfield with intermediate distance pass plays. The defensive style isn’t much different than has been fielded in the past, but the line is bigger and a bit faster than we are used to. It still has problems with running quarterbacks, and the secondary has just not stiffened yet. That’s a concern for this one because Nardo has found a good quarterback, too, and as we saw in the recent past when he has a good quarterback his teams go from wobbly to competitive. To win this Tech has to drive and score on nearly every possession. The defense needs to get fast “A” gap pressure on Pitt’s QB, and the secondary needs to stiffen up considerably. It’s also going to need to avoid any “prevent” situations since Pitt can score fast if it needs to. Add all that stuff up, and this one is going to be one of two things. A runaway with one team dominating over the other with fast offensive and heavy defensive pressure, or both teams are going to force a tough close contest. I am thinking the latter is more likely, I still have pictures in the library of the 4th quarter 4th and Goal for Pitt at the Tech 2. This stacks up to be, in my mind anyway, a similar contest. I think Tech takes it, but it’s going to be close, a 3- or 4-point difference. Both teams are probably good for scores in the mid- to high- twenties. The team that breaks 30 wins. 31 - 24 Hokies Just a Reminder About Friday Evening If you are coming to the game, check your seat against the chart, and wear the appropriate color. picks.blurb: Virginia Tech final odds and prediction for Week 5 vs. Pittsburgh Skip to main content About Virginia Tech Hokies News Virginia Tech Football Virginia Tech Basketball FanSided NCAA Sites Virginia Tech Football Recruiting Hokies In the NFL Virginia Tech All-Time Football Lists Virginia Tech Basketball Recruiting Virginia Tech Women's Basketball After the Virginia Tech and Pittsburgh football teams have begun the season perfectly at 4-0, the two will face off on Friday night at Lane Stadium in Blacksburg in a massive primetime showdown that will have a lot of eyes on it. When the ball is kicked off, the two teams will make history as the only two undefeated Power 4 teams to meet this late in the season without either team being ranked . Virginia Tech head coach James Franklin and Pitt coach Pat Narduzzi don't care about that and are just focusing on winning the game. Whoever wins the game should be ranked in Sunday's Associated Press Top 25 poll. Let's take a look at the latest odds and make a prediction for the biggest game in almost a decade in Blacksburg. Virginia Tech vs. Boston College: Final odds, spread, and total Odds provided by DraftKings Sportsbook Virginia Tech (-162) Pittsburgh (+136) Virginia Tech -2.5 (-115) Pittsburgh +2.5 (-105) 54.5 (over -118/under -102) Virginia Tech vs. Pittsburgh Prediction This is an interesting matchup. This is Pittsburgh's first true road game of the season, as the first four games they have played have been at home against Miami of Ohio, Central Florida, Syracuse, and Bucknell. The Hokies have won home games against VMI and Old Dominion, as well as road games the last two weeks at Maryland and Boston College. The latter was played in a Nor'easter and required a fourth-quarter rally to remain undefeated. This is a matchup between two teams that have proven to have explosive offenses with young and talented quarterbacks. The question is going to come down to the defenses. Which unit will create more turnovers? Will Pitt's defensive line be a problem for Virginia Tech's patchwork offensive line? Will the Hokies' crowd affect the Panthers' offense, which is on the road for the first time in 2026? So many questions will be answered that will have an effect on the outcome. In the end, this is a complete toss-up, but the Hokies secondary has been struggling this season, and with Panthers QB Mason Heintschel, if he gets into a rhythm, it could be a long night for Brent Pry's crew. Heintschel went down during the Panthers' win over Virginia Tech on Friday night Imagn Images After the elation of their 35-33 victory on the road over Virginia Tech on Friday night, Pittsburgh received some unfortunate news on Saturday when testing revealed starting quarterback Mason Heintschel suffered a season-ending knee injury, sources told CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. An MRI revealed Heintschel suffered an ACL tear, sources said, and the 5-0 Panthers will now have to continue their season in pursuit of an ACC Championship without their starting quarterback. Heintschel leads the nation in touchdown passes with 14 this season, completing 66.2% of his passes for 1,304 yards and just one interception prior to suffering his injury on Friday night in Lane Stadium. In Heintschel's place, Holden Greiner stepped in and performed well for the Panthers. Greiner went 8-for-12 for 78 yards and a touchdown to lead Pitt to a thrilling victory to remain undefeated and position themselves firmly in the ACC Championship race. The Panthers figure to finally move into the top 25 this week, and the Panthers will look to lean on a defense that is 18th in the country in points allowed, averaging just 13.4 points per game to keep them in that position. Pitt will host North Carolina next Saturday in an effort to become bowl-eligible in the first six weeks of the season. The Panthers then go to Boston College and travel to Miami to face the ACC favorite Hurricanes, in what will be the biggest test for Greiner and the Panthers as they look to adjust after losing Heintschel. Daniel Yanofsky Sat, October 3, 2026 at 9:19 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Things were looking bright for the Pittsburgh Panthers this season. Mason Heintschel looked sharp early in his sophomore campaign, leading the team to a 4-0 record heading into a game against Virginia Tech. However, Pittsburgh's season may have taken a massive turn after Heintschel appeared to be injured against the Hokies. Carried off the field with what appeared to be a leg injury, Heintschel was forced to leave the game, which Pittsburgh won 35-33. Here are the latest updates on the status of the Panthers' star QB. Mason Heintschel was helped off the field by two trainers. The injury came during the Panthers' game against Virginia Tech after being taken down by two Virginia Tech tacklers. Attempting to run toward the right sideline on third down, Heintschel got hit by one tackler, and the other appeared to hit him later than expected. On October 3 , On3 reported Heintschel would get an MRI on his right leg. Coach Pat Narduzzi later said an update likely wouldn't be given until Monday morning. "There's nothing (update-wise)," Narduzzi said . "We're on the road. We'll probably give you an update on Monday morning, Monday at noon. Couldn't tell you." It wasn't until that Saturday afternoon that ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Heintschel tore his ACL and will miss the rest of the season. Pitt has not yet confirmed the report.

home.headline: Virginia Tech football's initial injury report brings both good and bad news
home.blurb: On Tuesday, the initial availability report for the Pitt game was released. Greene and Cunningham were listed as probable, while Terry was listed as out, something that wasn't a surprise after Franklin's comments on Monday . According to David Cunningham of Tech Sideline , Brody Meadows and Cunningham were participants in practice on Tuesday, but did not go through the one-on-ones against the defense. That is a sign that, despite being listed as probable, Cunningham might not go this week against the Panthers either. It's a short week for the Virginia Tech football team after they rallied in the fourth quarter for a 21-14 win last Saturday afternoon at Boston College. Trailing 14-6, the Hokies scored on back-to-back drives late for their first ACC win under James Franklin. The short week means everything moves up a day, including gameday to Friday night, when Virginia Tech hosts Pittsburgh in a battle of two 4-0 teams at Lane Stadium . Franklin and his staff are dealing with some injuries a third of the way through the season, and the initial availability report for Friday night's game was released, and it brought some promising news for the Hokies. Initial availability report brings mixed news for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt Last week, the Hokies were thin on offense. The week before, against Maryland, offensive lineman Justin Terry went down with an injury in the second quarter; wide receiver Ayden Greene did, too. Then, before the Hokies flew to Boston, offensive lineman Montavious Cunningham popped up on the injury report. That would be a big loss of a veteran lineman ahead of one of the biggest games in Blacksburg in years. That would force Franklin and offensive line coach Matt Moore to shuffle more for the game, and likely during it as well. That's less than ideal. As far as Greene goes, it sounds promising that he could play against Pitt, and that would be big for quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer and offensive coordinator Ty Howle. If not, Marlion Jackson should get more reps after he played against BC and hauled in a fourth-quarter touchdown reception that eventually led to a tie game after Jeffrey Overton Jr. added the two-point conversion. There are still a couple more days before kickoff, and the true test will be pregame warmups on Friday night. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Probable corresponds to "likely to play", offering roughly a 75% chance, per the ACC's explanation. Questionable means "uncertain to play", offering around a 50% chance, while doubtful corresponds to unlikely (25%). Out means the player will not play in the game, while a game-time decision (on game day only) means that the final decision will be made closer to the game itself. It's the second straight week that Virginia Tech has 13 players on the availability report: two are out, nine are questionable and two are probable. Northwestern will host Penn State in the first game at the new Ryan Field, a nearly $900 million venue that claims to be the most expensive college stadium ever built. There are plenty of Penn State storylines Friday night beyond a mostly new program getting proxy retribution for last year's loss at Beaver Stadium. Meanwhile, there's a big football game between Penn State (3-1) and Northwestern (2-1) teams that each lost their Big Ten openers, but in very different ways. The Wildcats held up well in an entertaining 29-23 fight at Indiana, and the Nittany Lions collapsed late in a 24-20 thriller against Wisconsin . Now, these two get a lovely place to play their important Friday night conference game. Penn State vs Northwestern: Quick Hits Penn State gets USC after this, followed up by a date at Michigan . Northwestern gets another home game against Ball State next, and then goes to Michigan State for a showdown against former head coach Pat Fitzgerald. A loss would make it the second year in a row that Penn State started 0-2 in the Big Ten and 3-2 overall. The Nittany Lions lead the nation in third down stops, allowing teams to convert just 19.2% of their chances. Northwestern is okay offensively on third downs, but the defense allowed Indiana to convert 60% of their tries. Northwestern doesn't live off forcing mistakes, but it needs them in this. However, Penn State turned it over just once and has only been flagged 19 times in four games. Why Northwestern Will Win Aidan Chiles has been wonderful. The transfer quarterback from Michigan State was amazing over the last two games against Colorado and Indiana, completing over 75% of his passes with five touchdowns and no picks. He might not be running like he normally does, but his slippery style should be a problem for a Penn State defense that's not doing much to get into the backfield so far. The Nittany Lions have only come up with six sacks so far. Penn State vs Northwestern Prediction, Betting Lines Penn State's offense was terrific over the first three games, but that was against Marshall, Temple , and Buffalo. It'll come out sharp with the midrange passing game, but the running game that's been missing against everyone but Temple won't get the invite to the party. The Nittany Lion defense will hold up well in a tough fight, the offense will pull off a big late scoring drive, and … Northwestern will walk it off with Jackson Kleather – he has yet to miss a kick – hitting the game-winner. picks.headline: Week 5 Game Predictions: Northwestern Wildcats vs. Penn State
picks.blurb: Week 5 Game Predictions: Northwestern Wildcats vs. Penn State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB March Madness Get Fantasy Plus NFL Power Rankings Rays top sloppy Yankees Week 5 Waiver Wire Falcons run over Saints White Sox up 2-0 in ALDS Week 5 Game Predictions: Northwestern Wildcats vs. Penn State Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Northwestern will return home Friday night when the Wildcats take on Penn State in the highly anticipated first game at New Ryan Field . Northwestern enters the matchup with a 2-1 record after falling just short in a 29-23 loss to No. 5 Indiana , while Penn State comes to Evanston at 3-1 after suffering a 24-20 loss to Wisconsin. The Wildcats will look to bounce back from their first loss of the season while beginning a new era in front of a large crowd. Penn State will also be looking to get back in the win column after allowing a 17-0 lead to slip away against the Badgers. The game is scheduled for 7 p.m. CT Friday at New Ryan Field and will air nationally on FOX. Here are our predictions for Friday's historic matchup. Alex Kwiatkowski (3-0): Northwestern 30, Penn State 24 I'm taking Northwestern to open the new Ryan Field era with a win. The Wildcats are starting to look like a team that can truly compete in the Big Ten. Northwestern entered last week as a 23.5-point underdog against No. 5 Indiana but nearly pulled off the upset, eventually falling 29-23 in Bloomington. What impressed me most was how Northwestern responded after a terrible first half. The Wildcats trailed 12-0 at halftime but refused to go away, scoring 23 points in the second half and putting themselves in position to potentially win the game late. Aidan Chiles continues to look comfortable in Chip Kelly's offense, and Northwestern has shown it has multiple weapons in the passing game. Chiles threw for 293 yards and accounted for three touchdowns against Indiana, while Luke Dehnicke and Griffin Wilde combined for 196 receiving yards. Sep 25, 2026; Bloomington, Indiana, USA; Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Aidan Chiles (0) scores a touchdown against Indiana Hoosiers linebacker Kaiden Turner (14) during the second half at Merchants Bank Field at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Now, Northwestern gets to return home with plenty of excitement surrounding the program. Friday will mark the first game at New Ryan Field, and the stadium is sold out. I expect the Wildcats to feed off the energy and come out hot in front of what should be one of the best home atmospheres Northwestern has experienced in years. Penn State, meanwhile, enters at a low point after blowing a 17-0 lead in a 24-20 loss to Wisconsin. The Nittany Lions will be motivated to bounce back, but I think Northwestern carries its momentum from the second half against Indiana into Friday night. I expect Chiles and the offense to put points on the board early, while the defense does enough to keep Penn State from finding a consistent rhythm. Northwestern begins its new era with a statement win. Prediction: Northwestern 30, Penn State 24 Nick Meyer (2-0): Penn State 27, Northwestern 24 The Wildcats looked like a Big Ten title contender on the road against Indiana last week, while Penn State was upset at home by Wisconsin. I expect Northwestern to be fired up for the opening game at New Ryan Field, but I also expect the Wildcats to make a few mistakes due to the emotions and jitters surrounding such a historic night. This should be another close game, but Northwestern is expected to be without tight end Luke Dehnicke, who had a huge performance against Indiana with seven receptions for 140 yards. His absence would take away one of Aidan Chiles' most productive targets. This is a winnable game for Northwestern, but I expect Penn State to have the advantage in the trenches on both sides of the ball. Ultimately, that will be enough for the Nittany Lions to escape Evanston with a close win. Prediction: Penn State 27, Northwestern 24

picks.blurb: Penn State Given Interesting Prediction Ahead of Northwestern Matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB March Madness Get Fantasy Plus NFL Power Rankings Rays top sloppy Yankees Week 5 Waiver Wire Falcons run over Saints White Sox up 2-0 in ALDS Penn State Given Interesting Prediction Ahead of Northwestern Matchup (Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images) Matt Levine Thu, October 1, 2026 at 8:17 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Penn State Nittany Lions will be looking to get back on track tomorrow against Northwestern , in what could be a tough game for the team. Penn State fell 24-20 to Wisconsin last week in what was one of the more surprising scores from the weekend. But the Nittany Lions believe that the loss to the Badgers was more of an outlier, and this team still has a lot to play for this year. As the team gets ready for the Wildcats, the Nittany Lions will need to make sure that they don't overlook them. Northwestern has played much better to start the season than they have in year's past, opening the year 2-1 under head coach David Braun. For Penn State, this can be a bounce-back game, with the team getting things right after the tough loss against Wisconsin. But Friday night games can be tough, especially having to go on the road. Heading into the game, the Nittany Lions are favored to win the contest, but not by too much. According to ESPN , Penn State is being given a 55.9 percent chance to take down Northwestern on the road. If the Nittany Lions are going to win this game, everything starts and end with quarterback Rocco Becht . Becht has looked good to open the year, throwing for 865 yards with nine touchdowns and one interception. But against the Badgers, Becht struggled, throwing for just 114 yards and one interception. The veteran signal-caller will need to get back on track in this game against Northwestern if the Nittany Lions are to have a shot at winning. Coming over from Iowa State with head coach Matt Campbell, Becht gives Penn State a legitimate option under center. But he has bene prone to some inconsistency at times during his career, and last week was one of those moments for him. Northwestern has its own star quarterback in Aidan Chiles , who transferred to the team this offseason. So far, Chiles has played very well for the Wildcats, throwing for 807 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions. If Penn State can find a way to slow him down, it could make life much easier to grab the win. But Chiles has turned this offense around, and this will be something that the Nittany Lions will need to focus on throughout the game. Overall, Penn State needs to take down Northwestern if they want a chance to make the College Football Playoff this year. The Nittany Lions are off to a good a start this year, even with the loss last week, and this game offers them a chance to turn the page.

The Nittany Lions will visit Northwestern on Friday evening as the Wildcats proudly open the doors to the newly renovated Ryan Field for the first time. That figures to make for a bit of a challenge as Northwestern will be fired up to show off their new digs and pick up a big win in conference play after an incredible effort last week on the road against Indiana. On the other hand, Penn State is merely looking to rebound after a tough loss at home last week to Wisconsin that saw the Nittany Lions blow a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter. The optimism for Penn State on the road against Northwestern may have dipped in the span of the past week, for good and understandable reasons, but the staff at Nittany Lions Wire still seems to think Penn State will find a way to come out of the week with a win. Here are our final score and player of the game predictions for Penn State's Week 5 game against Northwestern, along with some brief thoughts on the matchup. Kevin McGuire, Lead Writer We saw last week that Penn State's offense really missed the likes of rising star wide receiver Koby Howard. This week, there can be no excuse for not having something going in the passing game. I think that means Rocco Becht needs to get into a comfort zone with his tight ends a bit more instead of looking for some big plays down the field from the receivers. So for the second week in a row, I'm looking for Ben BRahmer to be a difference maker for the offense. If Penn State can get that, then they should be in good enough shape to get out of Evanston with a hard-fought win. Northwestern will not make anything easy on the Nittany Lions. This may need to be a bit of a scrappy win from the offense. Final score prediction: Penn State 20, Northwestern 18 Player of the game pick: Ben Brahmer, Penn State tight end Paul White, Contributor This Northwestern team just took Indiana down to the wire, so I'd imagine a Penn State win would have to be in a close game. That doesn't sound like such a fun idea after last week's game, but hopefully we can keep our composure this time Final score prediction: Penn State 27, Northwestern 24 Player of the game pick: Chase Sowell, Penn State wide receiver Christopher Sheppard, Contributor The Nittany Lions find themselves in a similar position to last year as they face Northwestern after an inexplicable loss yet again. This time, it's on the road as Northwestern opens up the new Ryan Field. In order to spoil affairs, the Nittany Lions have to get going in the passing game and take advantage of what could be an aggressive Wildcat defense. Look for Chase Sowell to step up in the continued absence of Koby Howard and be the difference in a game that could come down to the last few plays. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . The Crimson Tide moved to 4-0 with a devastatingly dominant 49-18 win against South Carolina . Sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell was flawless with 365 yards passing and four touchdowns. Mississippi State is in the midst of one of the great starts in program history, reaching consecutive 4-0 starts for the first time since World War II. The Bulldogs came from behind to stun No. 19 Missouri 31-24 behind 360 yards and three touchdowns from superstar quarterback Kamario Taylor . Alabama has dominated the matchup between these two teams all-time, holding an 86-18-3 advantage, including a 40-17 win in 2023. However, the last MSU win came in Nick Saban's first season -- can the Bulldogs turn the Tide? Where to watch Alabama vs. Mississippi State live Date : Saturday, October 3 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Davis Wade Stadium -- Starkville, Mississippi TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Alabama vs. Mississippi State: Need to know Super Kamario: Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor has been the story of the early college football season. The Macon, Mississippi, native dreamed of playing in Starkville, and leads the SEC with 344.3 yards of offense per game. Taylor has thrown for at least three touchdowns in every start, including in road trips to Minnesota and South Carolina. With him in the lineup, suddenly anything seems possible at Mississippi State. Russell's rise: Taylor might be the best quarterback in the nation; he also might not be the best quarterback in this game. Since throwing a pair of interceptions in his first SEC start against Kentucky , Russell has been astonishing, throwing for 685 yards and seven touchdowns on 77% completion in wins over Florida State and South Carolina. Behind Russell's explosion, Alabama leads the nation in points per game against Power Four competition at 48.0 points per game. Best on worst: With so much attention on the quarterbacks, the secondaries will take center stage. Mississippi State has the worst passing defense in the SEC statistically, but the Bulldogs rank ahead of the Tide in both yards per attempt and passer rating allowed. Mississippi State has recorded nine sacks in four games, but getting a consistent pass rush could change the game. Alabama vs. Mississippi State prediction, picks Mississippi State is ready for this moment, and there's a lot to like about the Bulldogs. Davis Wade Stadium will be packed. The Bulldogs have a better running game to surround Kamario Taylor. They've played more competitive games to build resilience. But like so many Alabama games before, the Tide will just find a way to pull away at the end in perhaps the best quarterback battle of the season. picks.headline: Mississippi State vs. Alabama Prediction, TV Channel, Kickoff Time, Everything Fans Need to Know
picks.blurb: Mississippi State vs. Alabama Prediction, TV Channel, Kickoff Time, Everything Fans Need to Know Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THINGS STATE SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS STARKVILLE — It's been nearly two decades since Mississippi State felt the joy of a win against Alabama. Sylvester Croom was roaming the sidelines as first-year coach Nick Saban and his Crimson Tide program were in the midst of a late season slide. Fast-forward 20 years and its Kalen DeBoer leading the way, looking to lead his team to 5-0 record for the first time in his tenure. On the flip side, Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby is looking to earn the first signature win of his young head coaching career while hosting No. 7 ranked Alabama for a nationally televised showdown on ABC. Here's everything you need to know to be prepared for what's a pivotal weekend for the Bulldogs program. Mississippi State Bulldogs running back Fluff Bothwell (24) and wide receiver Zion Ragins (7) react after a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Missouri Tigers at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Game Information Game Information Mississippi State vs. Alabama Crimson Tide When : Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026 Kickoff Time : 11 a.m. CT Venue : Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville, Mississippi TV Channel : ABC Radio : Bulldogs Sports Network Series Record : Alabama leads 86-18-3 Betting : Alabama (-5.5), O/u: 60.5 total points ( FanDuel ) DISCLAIMER : Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. What ESPN Thinks The brand of Alabama remains strong on the national radar and that's no different this week at ESPN with the Crimson Tide given a 74.2% chance of going into one of the most hostile atmospheres in all of college football and pulling out a win, according to ESPN's Football Power Index . Mississippi State State continues its climb up the FPI rating system, coming in this week at No. 9 among SEC teams and No. 20 overall with key victories on the road at Minnesota and South Carolina plus another against then No. 19 Missouri. This starts one of the stiffest stretches for any team as the Bulldogs are set for a murderer's row-level slate with Alabama coming Saturday, proceeded by a BYE, on the road at LSU, home against Oklahoma and then another road trip to Austin to face the Texas Longhorns. The Bulldogs chances of winning out are slim at 0.1%, but do have a 97.5% chance of at least reaching bowl eligibility with six wins. When it comes to making the playoffs, Lebby's team has the sixth-best odds SEC teams at 23.8% to at least make the field, 1.6% to make the championship game and 0.5% chance to win the national championship. ESPN FPI (SEC) Rankings 1. Georgia 2. Texas 3. Alabama 4. LSU 5. Florida 6. Tennessee 7. Texas A&M 8. Ole Miss 9. Mississippi State 10. Oklahoma 11. Auburn 12. South Carolina 13. Missouri 14. Kentucky 15. Vanderbilt 16. Arkansas Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer walks off the field after a victory against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What DeBoer Is Saying What DeBoer Is Saying One of the hardest things for a coach to prepare his team for in a road game at Davis-Wade Stadium is the cadence of cowbells. Thousands of cowbells. "Personally, this is one of those stadiums that I haven't played in no matter where I've been," DeBoer said Monday. "What I hear from the people that I trust, is that it's going to be an absolutely crazy environment. We're going to be prepared for that. We talked about as a team this morning and we're looking forward to that challenge. "We know, this week, we've got to work on that crowd noise. There will probably be a lot of cowbells that we're hearing in practice in one form or fashion. Another thing is that it's just an early game. It's an 11 o'clock kickoff. We're a morning practice team and we've had some success in those morning games. We've got to go on the road and travel that morning. It's going to be a little different set-up that way too." The Bulldogs' defense has been very active this season at stopping explosive plays and keeping everything in front of them. They're disciplined, bring elite energy and effort with each down. "They play complementary football. They get the ball back, get off the field and get the ball back to the offense. I think it's timely stops. It's a group effort of guys flying around. They're going to be multiple in what they show you. "I have a lot of respect for them and what they are doing this time of the year. I think complementary football is what they're doing really well at Mississippi State. They're explosive. Obviously, that defense has to face that offense every day in practice. It's high level across the board." Mississippi State Bulldogs head coach Jeff Lebby looks on during the second quarter against the Missouri Tigers at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What Lebby Is Saying What Lebby Is Saying The Crimson Tide offense is full of big play athletes at nearly every position. Whether that's done with Keelon Russell's dual-threat combination, a four-headed backfield, Ryan Williams or any other weapon, Lebby knows his defense has to play assignment-driven, technically sound football to avoid allowing the game to get away from them early. "We're gonna have to do a great job tackling," Lebby said. "That's gonna be a huge piece of it. He's played really well. He's been incredibly productive. There's been explosive plays. He's got great talent around him. And so for us it's going to be about applying pressure, getting our fans really involved and excited about what's going on in between those white lines. "So for us it's kinda like I mentioned. We gotta get him off the spot and we've got to do a great job taking air out of it on the back end and making the plays when we get the chance." Alabama is tied for No. 24 nationally in sacks with 11 on the season. On the otherhand, Mississippi State has given up nine sacks on the season, which ranks No. 9 nationally, but the most alarming number was the four given up against Missouri in last week's 31-24 victory. And Lebby knows the biggest key to the Bulldogs upset bid will be keeping star quarterback Kamario Taylor upright to further establish himself as a Heisman Trophy contender. “[We] had moments where we were really clean, and had moments where we’ve got to continue to clean up,” Lebby said. “The fundamental pieces of it I’m gonna continue to talk about. Those guys playing clean fundamentally gives us the best chance to protect 1, but there were issues from a game standpoint. picks.blurb: Former UCLA Coach Rick Neuheisel Predicts Winner of Alabama-Mississippi State Game Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS No. 7 Alabama (4-0, 2-0) travels to Davis Wade Stadium to face No. 16 Mississippi State (4-0, 2-0) in the SEC's lone ranked matchup of Week 5 (Noon EDT, ABC). These two programs are separated by an hour and a half's driving distance and are meeting for the first time in three seasons. Alabama and Mississippi State have been traditional staples on each other's schedules, although the 86-18-3 advantage held by the Crimson Tide makes for the most lopsided series in SEC history. The Bulldogs' last victory was in 2007, Nick Saban's first season in Tuscaloosa. The closest Mississippi State came within the last 16 meetings was in 2017; the game was tied in the final 30 seconds, and Jalen Hurts hit then-freshman wide receiver DeVonta Smith for a 26-yard touchdown pass to win it 31-24. The matchup features a pair of high-octane offenses Sep 26, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell (12) throws the ball during the first quarter against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alabama has scored 45 points or more in each of its first four games. The Crimson Tide did run back interceptions for touchdowns in three of those four, but that means the offense has scored no fewer than 38 points in a game to start the season. Alabama has scored 45 points or more in each of its first four games. The Crimson Tide did run back interceptions for touchdowns in three of those four, but that means the offense has scored no fewer than 38 points in a game to start the season. Keelon Russell has been fantastic for Alabama, but the most impressive part of the offense is the run game. The Crimson Tide has been questionable in that department for the better part of three seasons, and it has very quickly found a combination of offensive linemen and running backs to correct the deficiency. On the other side, Kamario Taylor has lived up to the hype for Mississippi State. He guided the Bulldogs to a pair of road wins at Minnesota and South Carolina to bring excitement to a fan base desperate for optimism, and he delivered a 31-24 win over Missouri to a packed Davis Wade Stadium under the lights in Week 4. Neuheisel: "I see two matchups here that are really cool." CBS Sports' "Inside College Football" panel predicted the winner of the game between Alabama and Mississippi State on Tuesday. Former UCLA head coach Rick Neuheisel pointed to a pair of critical matchups between the Crimson Tide and Bulldogs while making his game pick. "Number one is the quarterbacks," Neuheisel said . "These two guys are both going to play on Sundays, both have just unique frames. They're 19 years old and they're just getting started." Despite the intrigue in the quarterback matchup, Neuheisel pointed to the other matchup as a deciding factor due to the current weather forecast for Saturday. "The second matchup is between the two defensive coordinators," Neuheisel said. "Both have been head coaches: Kane Wommack was at South Alabama, Zach Arnett was ironically right here at Mississippi State, these guys know how to play field position defense. It's supposed to rain a lot during the game, I think I've got to go, in that situation with Alabama." Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: David Pollack Picks Winner of Alabama-Mississippi State Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Two of the best young quarterbacks in college football go head-to-head Saturday when No. 7 Alabama visits No. 16 Mississippi State. For that matter, two of the best teams in the country clash in Starkville, Mississippi, as the Crimson Tide (4-0, 2-0 SEC) and Bulldogs (4-0, 2-0) kickoff at noon ET on ABC in arguably the most compelling matchup of the day. College football analyst David Pollack dissected the matchup on his "See Ball Get Ball" podcast while noting the key factors that he believes will ultimately sway the game as Mississippi State and sophomore QB Kamario Taylor take on Alabama and redshirt-freshman QB Keelon Russell. "Man, these two quarterbacks, how exciting. Is there a better matchup for just some of the most talented guys in the country, some of the biggest playmakers, some of the young stars in the game that have just been putting up video game, stupid numbers?" Pollack said. "... It's been crazy to watch them. There's supposed to be a little bit of a learning curve." How Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor and Alabama's Keelon Russell stack up Mississippi State sophomore quarterback Kamario Taylor is one of the breakout stars of this 2026 college football season. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Taylor got a chance to flash his immense upside at the end of last season, making two starts as a true freshman. Taylor got a chance to flash his immense upside at the end of last season, making two starts as a true freshman. Against Ole Miss in late November, Taylor threw for 178 yards and an interception but rushed for 173 yards and 2 scores in a loss. Then in the Duke's Mayo Bowl vs. Wake Forest, he threw for 241 yards and a TD and rushed for 63 yards and a score. Now the full-fledged starter this season, Taylor has yet to fully unleash his rushing ability, taking off only as needed thus far with 37 attempts for 185 yards and a TD. But that component of his game is an ever-present threat to opposing defenses nonetheless. Meanwhile, he's showcased his arm talent in a major way, completing 69.2% of his passes for 1,192 yards, 14 TDs and 2 INTs. That included a season-high 360 yards with 3 TDs and 1 INT in a 31-24 win over Missouri last week. Your weekly dose of Kamario Taylor throwing a perfect deep ball🤩 (Via: SEC Network) pic.twitter.com/S0ZAp7gsST As for Russell, the redshirt-freshman has gotten better and better with each week this season. Since passing for just 188 yards with 1 TD and 2 INTs in a Week 2 win over Kentucky, Russell has found his comfort zone the last two weeks. He completed 23 of 30 passes for 320 yards, 3 TDs and 0 INTs along with 3 rushes for 56 yards and a score in a 50-36 win over Florida State and then went 21-of-27 passing for 365 yards, 4 TDs and 0 INTs plus another rushing TD in a 49-18 blowout over South Carolina. Overall, Russell has completed 70.9% of his passes for 1,129 yards, 8 TDs and 2 INTs with 168 rushing yards and 3 scores. Keelon Russell was making NFL THROWS all game long against South Carolina. Russell finished the game 21/27 (78%), for 365 passing yards, and 5 TOTAL TD’s. The Alabama QB is one of the most talented QB prospects in PROGRAM HISTORY 😳🔥 pic.twitter.com/LNwW4LIqJu "No teams feel better about their team moving forward for next season and for this season than Alabama and Mississippi State, so think about that," Pollack said. "They found their guys that are lightning in a bottle that can make plays with their feet, but both of them are athletic guys that play the quarterback spot." David Pollack makes his prediction for Alabama-Mississippi State Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell has passed for 1,129 yards, 8 TDs and 2 INTs through four games plus 3 rushing TDs. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As to the matchup Saturday, Alabama is a 5.5-point road favorite, per DraftKings Sportsbook . As to the matchup Saturday, Alabama is a 5.5-point road favorite, per DraftKings Sportsbook . Along with Taylor, Mississippi State is led offensively by running back Fluff Bothwell (402 rushing yards, 96 receiving yards and 4 totals TDs) and wide receivers Anthony Evans III (28 catches for 408 yards and 3 TDs) and Sanfrisco Magee (13-208-5). Bothwell is listed as probable for Saturday with an unspecified injury that is believed to be minor. Mississippi State ranks fourth nationally at 533.3 yards per game and 15th in scoring at 43.0 points per game. Defensively, the Bulldogs rank just 74th in yards allowed (353.8/game) and 52nd in scoring defense (21.0 PPG). For Alabama, Russell's top targets have been Ryan Coleman-Williams (17-333-3) and Lotzeir Brooks (17-256-1), while Daniel Hill leads an improved Crimson Tide rushing attack with 225 yards and 4 TDs on 4.9 yards per carry. Alabama ranks fourth nationally in scoring at 48.0 PPG and 24th in total offense (471.5 YPG), while ranking 47th in total defense (315.3 YPG) and 46th in scoring defense (20.3 PPG). Pollack ultimately gives Alabama the edge for a few reasons. "If I'm Kamario Taylor, I love what I have. I love my wide receivers. I love my running back. I love my system. I love my coach. I don't know that I love my offensive line, and specifically the left tackle spot," Pollack said. "It's an issue. It's a problem. It was last week time and time again. You're just watching holding penalty, holding penalty, turnstile. "Everything about me wants to pick Mississippi State, but it feels like the Kentucky [vs. Alabama] game to me a little bit. I don't know that Mississippi State can affect the passer enough. Can they get enough pressure? Can they get Alabama behind the chains? Can you get Keelon Russell to the ground? "I love the way Alabama is playing football right now. I just like it. I think the arrow is pointing way up, [the Crimson Tide is] becoming more physical in who they are and finding themselves. I like Alabama in this game -- I think it's 34-28. I think K1 is going to do his thing, he's going to make some plays, but it's just hard to pick against Alabama's talent, their whole team and Keelon Russell being able to go tit for tat with you and Alabama's defense making the degree of difficulty just a little too hard for a banged-up-slightly K1, a banged-up-slightly Bothwell. Those are two big issues in this game too that I'll be interested to see." Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. away.headline: Alabama's mounting injuries on defense may have been a blessing in disguise as talented true freshman bursts onto the scene
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: Griffin is getting more time in the lineup with Justin Hill and Desmond Zulu both out for the considerable future . So the immediate question became who would fill the void for Alabama’s defense. Griffin helped answer it in a big way. What stood out most was where Griffin lined up. He played stack backer, whether that was at the Mike or the Stinger, and he also spent time along the edge at the Bandit and Wolf positions for the Crimson Tide defense. Griffin was the highest-rated signee in Alabama’s 2026 class, and he has looked every bit of that. To be out there dominating as a true freshman tells you everything you need to know. This guy is going to be a problem for years to come. With two key defenders sidelined, the Alabama Crimson Tide turned to its highest-rated 2026 signee against Mississippi State. What he did on Saturday should change how Kalen DeBoer’s defense looks heading into a showdown with Georgia. Alabama’s win over Mississippi State on Saturday will be remembered as an offensive explosion. On the other side of the ball, though, the Crimson Tide got a breakout performance from true freshman linebacker Xavier Griffin. If not for injuries, that game may never have happened. Xavier Griffin vs. Mississippi State stats Xavier Griffin played all over the Alabama defense That’s a lot to put on a true freshman’s plate, and he handled all of it. Griffin finished the day leading the Crimson Tide with nine tackles. On top of that, he added a tackle for loss and a sack and a half. He was all over the football field against Mississippi State. Griffin is drawing a familiar comparison Griffin looked a lot like Jihaad Campbell did on Saturday. Maybe it’s the No. 11 and the build, but the versatility he brings to Alabama’s defense is insane. Few players can move from the second level to the edge and look comfortable doing both. That versatility is exactly why the Tide can’t afford to keep him on the sideline. Losing Hill and Zulu hurts, and nobody wants to see players go down. But because it forced Griffin into a bigger role, and now that he has shown what he can do, there’s no going back. Alabama needs Xavier Griffin on the field against Georgia The stakes go up in a big way this weekend when the Georgia Bulldogs come calling. Alabama is going to have to play its best game of the year to this point. There can’t be slow starts . There can’t be lapses in coverage in the secondary. There can’t be bad play calls. Against a team like Georgia, every mistake gets magnified. That’s where Griffin comes in. He needs to be on the field as much as possible, whether that’s chasing down ball carriers from the stacked backer spot or getting after the quarterback off the edge. Alabama is going to need every bit of juice it has against Georgia, and Xavier Griffin brings a lot of it. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. "Desmond, he's continued to work back, but he'll likely not be ready for this week, and probably a couple more weeks yet." "Justin, just working back from his lower-extremity injury, he'll be back this season too, but more than likely not this week." "And for him to get out there and get his feet underneath of him, I thought he did a nice job for his first, really, start, really from a volume standpoint, his most meaningful full reps. There's a high ceiling for him, for sure, and you can see that. "He's worked a couple of different positions, because throughout the year, throughout camp, we knew that he had that in him. But you're also trying to get him just settled in on one position and be really good at one spot. But got out there and did a nice job, and I thought both of them were integral to our success." For the first time this season, Michigan hits the road and travels to Minnesota to take on the Gophers. Michigan has dominated this series and the Wolverines have won the last five meetings against Minnesota. But that doesn't mean the Gophers are going to lay down, and P.J. Fleck's team believes they have what it takes to upset the Wolverines. And so do some national analysts. We have predictions from three different sites, and then we determine if there is major concern for Michigan this weekend. The four-man crew at Fox Sports is leaning toward Minnesota. There were three members who took the Gophers, with one analyst taking Michigan. RJ Young - Minnesota Laken Litman - Minnesota Michael Cohen - Minnesota "Even though Michigan has a 3-1 overall record, it feels like there is an undercurrent of dysfunction for the Wolverines. Expect the Gophers to score a second consecutive upset. " Ben Portnoy - Michigan Both Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer believe Michigan will go into Minnesota and get the job done. Chris Hummer: Michigan 27-20 "The value in this game is with Minnesota. The Gophers are 3-1 with a quality road win over Washington. Meanwhile, the Wolverines have played four games this season, and three of them have been decided by seven points or fewer. But … I think Michigan has found something with Bryce Underwood. He's played much better the last two weeks -- a 68% completion rate, a four-to-one touchdown-to-interception ratio -- and Michigan is by far the best defense the Gophers have seen this season. The Wolverines respond on the road." Brad Crawford: Michigan 27-20 On3's J.D. PicKell The former Cornell and Baylor wide receiver has Michigan rowing the boat in Minnesota. "I think Michigan off a loss and that offense trending upward a little bit dangerous. I like it going to Minnesota. I love row the boat. Fun expression. picks.blurb: 3 Predictions for Michigan Football Against Minnesota Skip to main content SI.COM MORE SPORTS NEWS SI.COM WOLVERINES FB SI.COM WOLVERINES BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Michigan Wolverines will take on the Minnesota Golden Gophers on Saturday in their first road game of the season. The Wolverines are reeling coming off a 20-19 loss at home to the Iowa Hawkeyes, and need to bounce back before the schedule at the end of the season gets daunting. This is not your father’s Minnesota team. They are tough, resilient, and playing good football after last week’s 27-24 win over the Washington Huskies. PJ Fleck may be a little odd, but he has his team playing well. Will that be enough to spring an upset over the Wolverines who are favored on the road? Here are some of our predictions for Michigan’s first road game of the season. Jordan Marshall Goes for 100 Yards Jordan Marshall says he’s good to go. We’re taking him at his word here, but the Michigan run game needs to find some traction. The Wolverines have been putrid on the ground this season, and rank 92nd in the nation in yards-per-game . Michigan’s task did not get any easier this week, as Minnesota’s run defense has been stingy to start the year. This is the type of defense where run plays need to have yards come after the running back is first contacted. When he is healthy, that is Jordan Marshall’s specialty. He gives the Wolverines a personality in their run game, and is a violent runner. Last week, it looked like he was getting on track and running as hard as he has all season before curiously being out of the game for the final possession. Marshall is going to be the man, he’ll have some short runs earlier that turn into long runs as Michigan plays into the body-blow theory. The bet here also is that Marshall breaks a run for an explosive gain, which the Wolverines have not had on the ground for one of their running backs this season. Marshall tops the century mark for the first time for any Wolverine rusher this season. Michigan Defense Gets 3 Takeaways Where are the takeaways? Michigan’s defense has been great in almost every metric this season, but have been unable to take the ball away enough. The Wolverines had two takeaways against Oklahoma, and one against UTEP. That’s it so far this season, and their offense has been too sloppy with the ball. The result is that Michigan is currently minus-3 in the turnover margin. Yes, Michigan needs to play cleaner on offense, but their defense needs to start making some plays as well. MICHIGAN PICKS IT OFF! 🤯 #Michigan cornerback Jyaire Hill comes up with a clutch interception to put the Wolverines in the red zone! pic.twitter.com/QaalnVgmLD Drake Lindsey has a chance to be an NFL quarterback when his college career is over, but he has some arm arrogance to him. That’s a compliment, but also means he might put the ball in harm’s way. The bet this week is Michigan picks off two passes and gets a strip sack from someone we’re predicting as the star of the game. Tariq Boney is the Star of the Show Whether John Henry Daley plays or not, he’s likely to play on a reduced snap count thanks to a leg injury he suffered on the second-to-last play of last week’s game against Iowa. That will mean more snaps for the backup defensive ends. Tariq Boney has been productive whenever he has been on the field. He often reminds me of Chase Winovich during the 2016 season. Winovich did not play much on run downs, but was tasked with getting after the quarterback in obvious passing situations. That could be Boney’s role throughout the season, even if it’s not a perfect comparison between the two players. But that's what Michigan is going to attempt to do this weekend after suffering a 20-19 loss to Iowa in Week 4. In reality, Michigan still holds its own fate in its hands . And that starts this weekend. The Wolverines hit the road for the first time and Michigan travels to take on Minnesota . The Gophers are coming off an impressive win over Washington, on the road, last weekend. Both programs enter Week 5 with a 3-1 record. Michigan is 78-25-3 all-time against Minnesota and this meeting will mark the 100th meeting for the Little Brown Jug. The Wolverines have won the last five games against Minnesota, but that doesn't mean Michigan can take this game for granted. Minnesota is a lot like Iowa. Neither program usually wows you on the offensive side of the ball, but defense and physicality can win them games. Minnesota hasn't quite lived up to expectations since P.J. Fleck was hired, but the Gophers haven't been an easy out when playing in Minnesota. Kyle Whittingham said this week that he feels like his team is 0-4, not 3-1. With a bye week coming up for Minnesota, this would be a great stepping stone to turning those feelings around and seeing Michigan play a complete game against a respectable opponent. Today marks the 107th meeting in one of college football's oldest rivalries as Michigan faces Minnesota at Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. Kickoff is scheduled for noon ET on FOX, with the Wolverines favored by 5.5 points. Having won the last six matchups, Michigan is backed in my Michigan vs. Minnesota prediction and college football picks to keep the Little Brown Jug in Ann Arbor. TOP PICK Who will win Michigan vs Minnesota today? Pick: Michigan -5.5 The Michigan vs. Minnesota rivalry has been an ugly one for the Golden Gophers. Minnesota has won the Little Brown Jug just four times since 1968, while Michigan has taken it home on 44 different occasions (Michigan has covered in nine of the last 12 matchups). And though the Wolverines are coming off a tough loss to Iowa, I like them to cover -5.5 or better because of their defense. Michigan's stop unit ranks eighth in EPA per rush, 24th in EPA per pass, and 16th in available yards percentage (33.6%). Minnesota's inability to run the ball (103rd in EPA per rush) will put a lot on quarterback Drake Lindsey's plate, and his lack of mobility could be an issue against the Wolverines. Michigan's pass rush (assuming Dom Nichols and John Henry Daley play) is one of the best in the country, already boasting 12 sacks and 71 pressures . Michigan vs Minnesota Over/Under pick: Under 43.5 The Little Brown Jug game has hit the Over nine straight times, but Michigan's style of play should help break the trend, though I would only play the Under at 42.5 or better . The Wolverines have yet to score more than 19 points in a Power Four game this season, and they've yet to give up more than 20 points in any of their games, allowing just 14.8 ppg. Michigan has one of the best defenses in the country, ranked No. 9 by SP+ , but Minnesota has a pretty ferocious defense too. The Golden Gophers rank sixth nationally in havoc rate (23.7%) and should force QB Bryce Underwood into mistakes (his 5.4% turnover-worthy play rate is among the highest in the country). I predict the Wolverines to win 23-17. Michigan vs Minnesota combo Minnesota has long struggled to win the Little Brown Jug, and nothing has changed since Fleck took over. The Golden Gophers have kept the game within 20 points just once in the four matchups under Fleck. With both defenses ranking in the top 35 in net EPA per play, I'm expecting a slow, grind-it-out first half before Michigan pulls away late. Look for Wolverines wide receiver JJ Buchanan to be the X-factor. While this is Kyle Whittingham's first time in the rivalry, he's no stranger to winning rivalry games. As Utah's head coach, Whittingham went 11-6 in the Holy War against BYU. Michigan -5.5 First-half Under 21.5 Michigan vs Minnesota prop: Minnesota team total Under 18.5 Minnesota is averaging just 20 ppg against Power Four opponents, and Michigan's defense is by far the best it has faced this season. If Lindsey gets pressured, the Gophers could really struggle to move the ball with consistency. The Wolverines' defense is No. 8 in net EPA per play and No. 20 in pass success (37.4%), and will likely be focused on stopping the pass with how lackluster Minnesota's run game has been this season. An offense ranked 67th in success rate (45.2%) and 91st in net adjusted EPA per play is going to have trouble scoring more than 17 on Michigan. I like the Under on Minnesota's team total at 17.5 or better . Photo By - Reuters Connect. Minnesota Golden Gophers running back Darius Taylor (1) hurdles. There will be no love lost on Saturday when Michigan and Minnesota square off for the Little Brown Jug. My Michigan vs. Minnesota prop picks key on a few areas where the market may be off, including a favorable matchup for JJ Buchanan against this Golden Gophers secondary. Here are my college football picks and Michigan vs. Minnesota predictions as these teams meet on Oct. 3 at noon ET live on FOX. Best Michigan vs Minnesota props Prop pick #1: Darius Taylor Under 49.5 rushing yards Darius Taylor enters this game averaging just 3.0 yards per carry for the Minnesota Golden Gophers and only 2.53 yards after contact. Considering his season-high rushing total of 56 yards came against Eastern Illinois on 14 carries, I see very little path to him reaching 50 against this Michigan Wolverines defense. This unit ranks Top 20 nationally in EPA per rush (11th), early-down EPA per play (18th), and explosive run rate (13th) . Minnesota ranks 104th in rushing success rate and 113th in line yards , and Taylor's inability to consistently create extra yardage on his own makes this a strong Under play. I'd back it to 57%. Prop pick #2: JJ Buchanan Over 74.5 receiving yards JJ Buchanan's 16.4-yard average depth of target is more than seven yards deeper than Andrew Marsh's. While Marsh is better at creating after the catch, Buchanan is getting downfield primarily from the slot and consistently stressing secondaries. That's why I prefer Buchanan's total, especially with it sitting only 15 yards above Marsh's number. The Golden Gophers rank in the 30th percentile in explosive pass plays allowed , with 13 of 64 completions against them going for 20-plus yards. Buchanan has topped 90 receiving yards in three of four games. With Minnesota allowing 94.0 yards after the catch per game, he should have opportunities to create enough chunk plays to clear this number. I'll play this up to 54%. Prop pick #3: Jalen Smith Under 34.5 receiving yards Moving the ball is going to be difficult for this Minnesota offense, and Jalen Smith could struggle to clear 30 receiving yards. He's done so just once this season, going for 51 against Mississippi State. But that game also saw him run 46 routes. In his other three games, Smith ran 24 routes or fewer, and he's averaging just 1.07 yards per route this season . The Wolverines defense ranks 11th in passing success rate and 12th in yards per dropback . Smith's inability to generate big plays makes him a strong fade candidate in this matchup. I'm playing this one to 53%. Prop picks : 5-3, +1.83 units Odds are correct at the time of publishing and are subject to change. Not intended for use in MA. After losing four straight Little Brown Jug games under PJ Fleck, Minnesota looks to end its losing streak against Michigan on Saturday at noon ET (FOX). Michigan vs Minnesota combo Since 1968, the Michigan vs. Minnesota rivalry hasn't been much of a rivalry, with Minnesota going 44-4. Minnesota head coach PJ Fleck hasn't had any luck ending the Wolverines' dominance, either, losing all four games with the Little Brown Jug on the line. Under Fleck, the Golden Gophers haven't been very competitive, going 1-3 ATS and losing by an average margin of 40.2-17 — and my Michigan vs. Minnesota prediction expects Fleck to add another tick in the loss column. While the Wolverines just fell to Iowa on the final play, they outplayed the Hawkeyes and should have won by double digits. Even in the loss, the Wolverines allowed just 20 points, and seven of them came on a kick return touchdown. Michigan's defense is ranked No. 9 by SP+ and sits eighth in EPA per rush, 24th in EPA per pass, and 16th in available yards percentage (33.6%) . Considering Minnesota's inability to run the ball ( 103rd in EPA per rush ), the Wolverines can focus on stopping Drake Lindsey and win this one by 6+ points. Michigan vs Minnesota player prop combo If Michigan wants to retain the Little Brown Jug and cover the spread, it needs to stop Lindsey. Luckily, for the Wolverines faithful, Michigan has one of the best pass defenses in the country, led by veteran cornerbacks and a ferocious pass rush. The Wolverines' defense ranks 11th nationally in pass success rate (33.9%) , and its front seven has racked up 12 sacks and 71 pressures. That will make it difficult for Lindsey to throw for 215+ yards, something he's done just three times in his last 12 games. It will be hard for Michigan to get production through the air, too, but wide receiver JJ Buchanan is an X-factor. The Utah transfer has been the Wolverines' best player this season (he caught the Hail Mary against Western Michigan) and ranks top 12 nationally in receiving yards (396) and touchdowns (4) . Buchanan's size (6-foot-4) and ball skills (0 drops) should be a mismatch, especially near the end zone. But the biggest key to a Michigan win might be Bryce Underwood's mobility. In Jason Beck's system, the former five-star's legs have been utilized far more consistently. He's averaging 48 rushing yards per game and sits 10th among QBs in forced missed tackles (14). Minnesota's run defense has been underwhelming this season, ranking 107th in rush success rate (48.2%), so expect Underwood to be a large part of Michigan's run game. Michigan and Minnesota meet Saturday at 12 p.m. ET at Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN, for a Big Ten showdown. The Wolverines are fresh off a buzzer-beater loss to Iowa — allowing a 16-yard touchdown pass as time expired to put an end to their unbeaten season. Minnesota has been playing well early in 2026, with their only loss this fall coming against No. 16 Mississippi State. My Michigan vs. Minnesota anytime touchdown scorer predictions and college football picks take a look at a few players who have a chance to find the end zone on Saturday, Oct. 3, including a long-shot who is an under-the-radar goal-line option for the Golden Gophers. Best Michigan vs Minnesota touchdown picks Michigan touchdown pick: JJ Buchanan Playable to 43%. JJ Buchanan leads all Michigan players with four touchdowns in 2026, accounting for 80% of the team's receiving touchdowns . His 6-foot-4 frame makes him a strong red-zone option, while his speed and route-running ability give him big-play potential, as shown by his 49-yard reception against Iowa last week. Buchanan is one of just two Michigan pass-catchers with more than six targets this season. If the Wolverines score through the air, there's a good chance Buchanan is on the receiving end. Minnesota touchdown pick: Darius Taylor Playable to 51%. Michigan hasn't allowed a rushing score yet in 2026, but if any running back is capable of breaking that streak, it's Darius Taylor . Taylor has a bigger frame than Minnesota teammate T.J. Thomas, making him better equipped for short-yardage and goal-line work . We've already seen that role this season, with Taylor scoring three rushing TDs compared to one for Thomas, who broke free for a 71-yard score in garbage time against Akron a couple of weeks ago. Since he's consistently out-snapping Thomas through the first four weeks, Taylor also offers better value. First touchdown scorer pick: Jordan Marshall Playable to 17%. Jordan Marshall leads Michigan running backs in snaps, rushing attempts, rushing yards, and is tied for the team lead in rushing TDs . He's also the only running back with a sizable role who hasn't fumbled, which should continue to earn him opportunities at the goal line. Marshall has the big-play ability to score from outside the red zone, with at least one 15+ yard run in three of his four games this fall. Expect him to be among Michigan's top options to find the end zone. Long-shot touchdown pick: Drake Lindsey Drake Lindsey hasn't scored a touchdown yet in 2026, but he found paydirt four times in 2025 and has a history of being used near the goal line . Michigan has held Oklahoma to 3.4 yards per carry and Iowa to 2.4 ypc this season, with neither team scoring a rushing TD against the Wolverines. To counter this, the Golden Gophers should opt for a tush push Saturday. Michigan vs Minnesota touchdown combo: Bryce Underwood + Drake Lindsey Playable to 8%. Bryce Underwood is a weekly threat to score with his legs. He's 6-foot-4 and 230 pounds, which makes him a quality option on quarterback sneaks and tush pushes . Underwood also has the speed to break a big run if the defense loses track of him, which we saw when he scored from the 38-yard line against Oklahoma. Lindsey has a similar build to Underwood, and I expect both of these QBs to put their body on the line in short-yardage situations.
