Michigan vs Minnesota Odds, Spread Michigan vs Minnesota point spread : Michigan -5.5 (-112), Minnesota +5.5 (-108) Michigan vs Minnesota over/under : 43.5 (-108o / -112u) Michigan vs Minnesota moneyline : Michigan -220, Minnesota +175 I am so unimpressed with Michigan . Not to beat a dead horse, but this team should be 2-2 after sneaking past Western Michigan in the first game, and then falling to Iowa in a buzzer-beater last week. In between those two games, the Wolverines also beat Oklahoma by the mere score of 17-10. The run game is probably the most unspectacular aspect of Michigan's game. Leading rusher Jordan Marshall is fine, but his 4.3 yards per carry is hardly moving mountains, and quarterback Bryce Underwood has only two fewer rushing yards than him. Speaking of Underwood, I've also expected better from a number-one overall recruit from his class – especially given the payday that he received to play in Ann Arbor. He has formed a great chemistry with JJ Buchanan, who leads the team in receiving on just under 20 yards per catch, along with Andrew Marsh, who leads in receptions. But that's where the problem lies. Buchanan and Marsh account for 71% of Michigan's receptions combined, and because of that, opponents know where Underwood is looking. It's either Buchanan, Marsh, or he'll take it for himself. On the defensive side of the ball is where the Wolverines thrive at a high level. Against the pass, they're ranked 13th in Success Rate allowed in pass plays, and ninth in Success Rate allowed in pass downs. Additionally, they do a high-end job at stuffing the run, ranking 13th in the FBS in opponent rushing yards allowed per game. PJ Fleck is a madman. I can't get the visual of him wiping a bloody nose off one of his players and draping it on his face out of my head. A true sicko. The Gophers are looking to secure their first home win over Michigan since 1977, and last week's win against Washington proved that they can do it. Michigan is vulnerable after losing to Iowa at the last second, and I think this is one of the rare times that Minnesota has the upper hand here. Minnesota likes to wear down its opponents, as showcased in Seattle last week. Its one loss was suffered against Mississippi State , one of the most dynamic teams in college football. Quarterback Drake Lindsey has been pretty efficient in his second season as the starter, completing passes at a 66% rate with seven touchdowns and two picks. And so far, he's revived the chemistry he formed with Javon Tracy last season, while seamlessly connecting with Cincinnati transfer Noah Jennings. In a complete 180, Minnesota doesn't like to run the ball a lot, ranking 134th in rushing attempts per game. A total shock, considering that Fleck likes to establish the run. TJ Thomas has been a total stud for the Gophers, rushing for 7.1 yards per carry and helping them achieve a 43rd Rush Play Success Rate. Defensively, this team does a fine job at holding down the fort. Fleck promoted Danny Collins as the defensive coordinator, and currently, the Gophers rank sixth overall in Havoc and 50th overall in points allowed. Did it seem like I was too harsh on Michigan? Because I thought I took it lightly on the maize and blue. I think this is a fascinating matchup because Michigan's defense has been stellar, but I wonder how the Wolverines fare on the offensive side. You also have to imagine that Huntington Bank Stadium is going to be rocking. Obviously, Minnesota not beating Michigan at home since the 70s is an alarming stat. After all, the Gophers have either been just good or dumpster fire bad since the early 1940s. Our projections have Michigan winning this game by 10 points, and it's for very good reason. However, while Michigan has the better team on paper, I feel like Minnesota is the one riding the momentum. That's why I'm taking the points with the Gophers. Chirp me on X if you must, because if this doesn't hit, I at least want to feel something. Pick: Minnesota +5.5

away.headline: Michigan's initial injury report for Minnesota game is quite concerning
away.blurb: The Michigan football injury report against Minnesota , at least the first report that came out on Wednesday had some surprises and raises some concerns. The Gophers will be a challenge. Michigan could also be without some of its best players. We knew John Henry Daley was going to be questionable . However, Andrew Marsh, who went over 100 yards last week, suddenly popped up on the injury report as questionable, which is essentially 50/50 that he will play. Andrew Sprague is also questionable. He's been out the past two weeks. Blake Frazier did a great job moving over to the right side in his absence. Frazier was injured against Iowa too, but he's probable for the Minnesota game. That's the one piece of good news. It's actually good news that Henry Daley is questionable. After he had a season-ending injury back in November, it's good to see he still has a chance to play this week. Dominic Nichols is also listed as questionable, which was his status last week, too. The arrow is pointing up. Hopefully, one of his top targets, Marsh, will be available on Saturday against Minnesota. Michigan, 3-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Iowa last Saturday, has to go through one more week before a bye week and a chance to rest up. In the meantime, Michigan has a challenging road game against the Golden Gophers, who knocked off Washington 27-24 last week. Thoughts on Michigan football injury report The idea of losing Marsh this week is a little scary. We all saw how difficult it was for Iowa to take away Marsh and JJ Buchanan. It was basically impossible. If the defense focused on one receiver or the other, Michigan just went the other way. There are plenty of other talented pass catchers to turn to. Salesi Moa and Travis Johnson have flashed as freshman. Channing Goodwin has experience, too. It would be nice if the Wolverines got Sprague back in the lineup. Link has done a solid job. Iowa has one of the better defensive lines in the Big Ten. Yet, Michigan was able to run for over 150 yards and only gave up one sack. The offense has struggled to score points, though, failing to reach 20 in three of the first four games. Iowa and Oklahoma aren't an average defense. Beyond that, Michigan was a play away from winning both games thanks to the improved play of Bryce Underwood. home.headline: Michigan's initial injury report for Minnesota game is quite concerning
home.blurb: The Michigan football injury report against Minnesota , at least the first report that came out on Wednesday had some surprises and raises some concerns. The Gophers will be a challenge. Michigan could also be without some of its best players. We knew John Henry Daley was going to be questionable . However, Andrew Marsh, who went over 100 yards last week, suddenly popped up on the injury report as questionable, which is essentially 50/50 that he will play. Andrew Sprague is also questionable. He's been out the past two weeks. Blake Frazier did a great job moving over to the right side in his absence. Frazier was injured against Iowa too, but he's probable for the Minnesota game. That's the one piece of good news. It's actually good news that Henry Daley is questionable. After he had a season-ending injury back in November, it's good to see he still has a chance to play this week. Dominic Nichols is also listed as questionable, which was his status last week, too. The arrow is pointing up. Hopefully, one of his top targets, Marsh, will be available on Saturday against Minnesota. Michigan, 3-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Iowa last Saturday, has to go through one more week before a bye week and a chance to rest up. In the meantime, Michigan has a challenging road game against the Golden Gophers, who knocked off Washington 27-24 last week. Thoughts on Michigan football injury report The idea of losing Marsh this week is a little scary. We all saw how difficult it was for Iowa to take away Marsh and JJ Buchanan. It was basically impossible. If the defense focused on one receiver or the other, Michigan just went the other way. There are plenty of other talented pass catchers to turn to. Salesi Moa and Travis Johnson have flashed as freshman. Channing Goodwin has experience, too. It would be nice if the Wolverines got Sprague back in the lineup. Link has done a solid job. Iowa has one of the better defensive lines in the Big Ten. Yet, Michigan was able to run for over 150 yards and only gave up one sack. The offense has struggled to score points, though, failing to reach 20 in three of the first four games. Iowa and Oklahoma aren't an average defense. Beyond that, Michigan was a play away from winning both games thanks to the improved play of Bryce Underwood. home.blurb: Please allow enough time to contact them especially during their limited weekend hours. The Gophers’ offensive line will be a patchwork unit for the rest of 2026 as starting center Ashton Beers has been ruled out with a season-ending injury, a source told the Pioneer Press on Wednesday. Beers was officially listed as out on Minnesota’s first unavailability report going into the Michigan game on Saturday, but the severity of the injury will cause the 6-foot-6, 320-pound lineman to miss all eight remaining games. He appeared to suffer an injury to his lower right leg during the 41-7 win over Akron on Sept. 12. The senior from Slinger, Wis., returned to play against the Zips and was initially listed as questionable for Washington game last Saturday before ultimately being ruled out ahead of the 27-24 win over the Huskies in Seattle. OSU lost to Miami in the quarterfinals last season, but quarterback Julian Sayin has a full season under his belt and he's throwing to the current Heisman Trophy favorite, receiver Jeremiah Smith . The junior has at least 150 receiving yards in three of the four games (he had 85 in a rout of Kent State ). That includes 217 in last week's 42-19 victory against Illinois , when Ohio State outgained the Illini 527-134. Sayin threw for 364 yards and four touchdowns, all to Smith. The quarterback also ran for 29 yards, while running backs Ja'Kobi Jackson and Bo Jackson both topped 50 as the Buckeyes rushed for 151. The OSU offense leads the Big Ten in total yards per game, averaging almost 100 yards more than Iowa (522-429), while both of these defenses are tough to crack. Iowa leads the Big Ten in allowing just eight points per game, while OSU yields 12.3 (fifth). The Buckeyes led the nation in scoring defense over the full season in 2025 (9.3 per game) while Iowa was eighth in FBS (16.1), so this is a continuation of that dominance. The Buckeyes have seven sacks, led by Riley Pettijohn and Kenyatta Jackson Jr . with two each, and six takeaways. Ten defensive players have at least 10 tackles, led by safety Earl Little Jr.'s 23. Jackson is part of a stacked defensive line that had 35 sacks last season (T-21 in FBS) and helped the defense lead the nation against the pass, allowing less than 130 yards per game. The Hawkeyes also are built on defense, as they are 10th in the nation in yards allowed (239.8 per game), while OSU is 27th (274.3). The Wolverines did manage to outgain the Hawkeyes 429-285, but Iowa got a key interception at their own 2-yard line in the third quarter. UM scored twice in four trips to the red zone, while Iowa scored on both drives inside the 20. Quarterback Hank Brown got off to a slow start but rallied the Hawkeyes to get his first road victory as a starter. Braeden Jackson's 99-yard kickoff return surely made a huge difference, but Brown completed 13 of his final 19 passes. Brown is completing 68% of his passes with 700 passing yards and five TDs on 97 attempts. The Hawkeyes also have four running backs with at least 125 rushing yards, led by Kamari Moulton with 293, He is averaging 7.3 yards per carry, while Jackson averages a team-high 9.3 and Xavier Williams averages 8.8 and has three TDs on just 16 carries. Iowa has nine sacks, led by end Joseph Anderson with two, and the defense has taken the ball away six times. Iowa is 12-4-1 against the spread since the start of last season, going 5-0-1 ATS against ranked teams and 2-0 ATS as a home underdog. The Buckeyes are 13-4-1 ATS since the beginning of 2025, including the College Football Playoff, 5-1 ATS as the road team and 8-3 ATS in Big Ten games. OSU is 7-11 to the Over during that same span, with all six road games and all six against ranked opponents going Under. The Big Ten showdown brings a moment of tension for Ohio State, which suffered a 55-24 loss during its last visit to Kinnick Stadium in 2017. With one loss already, the Buckeyes can ill-afford a stumble as they enter a month that also includes trips to No. 6 Indiana and No. 18 USC . For Iowa, this represents a breakthrough opportunity on the heels of a last-second win at Michigan in Week 4. That victory propelled Iowa to 4-0 for the first time since 2021, when the Hawkeyes rose all the way to No. 2 in the AP poll on their way to an appearance in the Big Ten Championship Game. Beating the Buckeyes would put Iowa on a similar trajectory and send its playoff chances skyrocketing. Ohio State won the last two meetings by 28 (2024) and 44 (2022), but there are signs that these Hawkeyes are better equipped to stage a competitive battle as these Big Ten stalwarts square off in Iowa City for the first time in nearly a decade. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Iowa live Date : Saturday, Oct. 3 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Kinnick Stadium -- Iowa City, Iowa TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com , CBS Sports App Streaming on Paramount+ Premium Ohio State vs. Iowa: Need to know Iowa's offensive punch: Iowa ranks No. 48 nationally in total offense entering this showdown, which is hardly remarkable on the surface. But after ranking 117th or worse in total offense for the past five seasons, it's a marked improvement. The Hawkeyes struggled to run the football against Michigan last week, but quarterback Hank Brown led a game-winning drive capped by a touchdown pass to Reece Vander Zee on the game's final play. Considering the hostility of Michigan Stadium and the quality of the opponent, it was the sort of clutch, late-game execution that would have been unfathomable for the Iowa offense at any point over the past several years. Ohio State's defensive questions: Ohio State ranks just 27th in total defense through four games, down from finishing the 2025 season at No. 1 in that metric. Considering seven players from last season's defense were selected in the 2026 NFL Draft , it's not shocking that the Buckeyes have dropped off a bit. But the slide came with a cost in a Week 2 loss at Texas , when Ohio State's defense couldn't get off the field over the final 20 minutes as the Longhorns rallied from a 23-3 deficit to win 24-23. Illinois racked up 462 yards and 25 first downs on Ohio State last week. Though the Buckeyes won 42-19, it wasn't a banner day for coordinator Matt Patricia's defense, which comes into this game with some questions to answer. Jeremiah Smith making history: Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith is on a blistering pace with 33 receptions for 617 yards and seven touchdowns through four games. The junior star is one touchdown away from tying Chris Olave for most receiving touchdowns in program history and just five away from matching ex-Michigan star Braylon Edwards for most receiving touchdowns in Big Ten history at 39. Smith is on track to become the first player to ever lead the Big Ten in receiving yards three times. He's also likely to surpass K.J. Hill and Emeka Egbuka for most receptions in Ohio State history in the near future. picks.blurb: Ohio State on SI Week 5 Picks: Can Ohio State Ruin Iowa's Early Momentum? Skip to main content SI.COM 2025 Football Bracket Buckeyes In the NFL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES BB The Ohio State Buckeyes were in cruise control, dominating the Illinois Fighting Illini with a 42-19 thumping in Columbus last Saturday. The victory was enough for the Illini to dismiss their defensive coordinator, Bobby Hauck, in a mutual parting of ways. Now No. 5 Ohio State turns its attention to a ranked-vs.-ranked matchup with the No. 14 Iowa Hawkeyes. The Buckeyes (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) are visiting their first hostile Big Ten environment at Kinnick Stadium, which will have much fanfare as College GameDay returns to Iowa City for a highly anticipated reunion. The game marks Ohio State’s first true Big Ten road test, as the Hawkeyes (4-0, 1-0 Big Ten) railed to secure a 20-19 last-second win over the Michigan Wolverines in Week 4. So far, the Ohio State on SI staff has hit more than 70 percent of its predictions this season. Can we see more of the same come Saturday? Check out our picks below to find out more. Ohio State vs. Iowa Game Details & Predictions Oct 5, 2024; Columbus, OH, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day shakes hands with Iowa Hawkeyes head coach Kirk Ferentz following the NCAA football game at Ohio Stadium. Ohio State won 35-7. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Date: Saturday, Oct. 3 Date: Saturday, Oct. 3 Time: 3:30 p.m. ET/12:30 p.m. PT TV Channel: CBS (consult TV Guide or preferred streaming provider for details). Odds: Ohio State -14 ; over/under is 45.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Location : Kinnick Stadium – Iowa City, Iowa Ohio State’s record under Ryan Day : 85-13 (8-6 in postseason bowl games/CFP). Last time vs. Iowa: A 35-7 home win on Saturday, Oct. 5, 2024. The game marks the 21st all-time meeting between the two programs, with the Buckeyes winning 17 of those matchups since Nov. 1989. Pregame festivities: College GameDay will be on-site in Iowa City for the first time since 2006. Ohio State so far this season: 3-1 (1-0 Big Ten) Zain Bando : 4-0 Dylan Buganski: 3-1 Rafael Zamorano : 3-1 Chip Minnich: 2-0 (began contributing ahead of Week 3) Zain Bando: Ohio State 38, Iowa 21 Ohio State’s first conference road game is a big one. Iowa has gotten off to a fast start behind a stingy defense, an ever-improving offensive line, plus has maintained the excellence that one would expect from a Kirk Ferentz team. Ferentz admitted this week that his team must play as close to flawless football as possible. That’s easier said than done when examining Ohio State. The Buckeyes have rolled all but one opponent (the Texas Longhorns) offensively, and even then, they had a 20-point lead in the fourth quarter before the defense collapsed, leading to a stunner in Austin nearly a month ago in a one-point loss. If Ohio State can get into an early rhythm, it should be an exciting afternoon with plenty of points and key defensive stops at the Hawkeyes’ expense, leading to a huge road win to begin a gauntlet stretch of Big Ten football. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 31, Iowa 17 Look for a slugfest. Put it another way - Iowa is going to make sure Ohio State is "Iowaed" by the time this game concludes. Longtime Iowa defensive coordinator Phil Parker will do whatever he can to eliminate explosive plays like the kind Illinois gave up to Ohio State last week, so that is going to require Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith and Coach Ryan Day to become creative with other outlets on the Ohio State offense. While it may not be pretty, and it may be stress-inducing, I like Ohio State to pull away in the fourth quarter. Rafael Zamorano: Ohio State 34, Iowa 24 The No. 5-ranked Ohio State Buckeyes are facing more than just a trap game for their Saturday date with the Iowa Hawkeyes at Kinnick Stadium. This foe must be taken seriously after taking down No. 18 Michigan at Ann Arbor last weekend. Luckily for the Buckeyes, their best player -- wideout Jeremiah Smith -- is coming off a whale of a game, including a personal-best four touchdowns against Illinois last weekend. Quarterback Julian Sayin also had one of his finest games with the program with 367 passing yards, his second-highest total ever, and a personal record tying four touchdown passes. Iowa has recently carved out a nice little niche as a defensive back school, and this year’s roster features the versatile Zach Lutner as a wildcard that can line up pretty much anywhere, along with Deshaun Lee and Jaylen Watson out on the corners. Smith against this unit will be the matchup to follow closely. Ohio State, nonetheless, should be able to avoid the upset and keep the ball rolling, coming back from Iowa City with a victory. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 24, Iowa 13 The last time Ohio State traveled to Kinnick Stadium to face the Kirk Ferentz-led Hawkeyes, the Buckeyes did not fare well. As I do not see this game being the prettiest victory for coach Ryan Day, it should look a lot different than what occurred on Nov. 4, 2017, when Iowa handed Ohio State its biggest loss in the last century. This should be the biggest test of consistency up to this point for quarterback Julian Sayin and this offense, as Iowa should do a much better job of keeping track of Jeremiah Smith and make Sayin able to spread the ball around to other weapons and test the offensive line in establishing a run game. Offensively, Ohio State’s defense should be able to stutter Iowa's attack. Iowa’s run game has struggled against Power 5 opponents, but so has Ohio State’s run defense. That will be a battle to watch. Also, Iowa’s offense benefits greatly from creating big-play opportunities and the Buckeyes gave up many to Illinois at home last weekend. I expect a gritty game that stays within one score heading into the fourth quarter, with Ohio State scoring early in the fourth to make it two scores, and the defense should put up a strong showing down the stretch to give Ohio State its first ranked win of the season. If the Iowa Hawkeyes want to knock off Ohio State, things are going to have to break their way, but they also have to do their part in managing this game perfectly. It isn't just hoping to get the right bounce of the ball or be on the receiving end of a tipped pass like last week against Michigan. It requires some serious focus and attention, which is an area Iowa is an expert in. Kamari Moulton rushes for 100 yards Iowa knows it has to mitigate how many possessions Ohio State gets this week to stick around in this game and to keep the defense fresh. The Hawkeyes are going to give a heavy dose of running the ball to ensure that's the case. Kamari Moulton should be fresh after just 13 carries against Michigan last week. Expect Tim Lester and the offense to ask a lot of Moulton in this one. It may not be a consistent barrage of five yards on each touch. It is likely to be a case of banging into a brick wall for two and three yards at a time before Kamari Moulton pops a few chunk plays. Jeremiah Smith is held under 100 receiving yards Jeremiah Smith has been held under 100 yards just once this year. It wasn't by a bad game. Against Kent State, he had five receptions for 85 yards in a 59-3 win. It was to keep him healthy. His other games? He has had games of 151 yards, 164 yards, and 217 yards. He is doing whatever he wants, whenever he wants, against defenses. Phil Parker has been around the block once or twice before, and he has tried to contain stars before. Iowa is likely to throw the kitchen sink at Smith with double coverage, or safety help at the least, to force other Buckeyes' wide receivers to step up. Iowa forces at least 2 turnovers The Hawkeyes' defense knows they have to steal possessions in this game and create short fields for the offense. That's not meant as an indictment of the offense. Instead, it's a compliment to Ohio State. The Buckeyes are explosive, and taking the ball away from them is going to be key for Iowa this week. I expect Iowa to be hyper-aggressive in punching at the ball to force a fumble this week on each run play. If Iowa can steal a short field and translate that into three or seven points, with the clock running, that's a gigantic win for the Hawkeyes. Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: David Pollack Picks Winner of Ohio State-Iowa Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS The biggest game of the week in the Big Ten is No. 14-ranked Iowa hosting No. 5 Ohio State in Iowa City on Saturday. The Hawkeyes are traditionally tough to beat at home in Kinnick Stadium, but the Buckeyes are 17-3 all-time in the series and 6-1 vs. Iowa over the last 20 years with the lone loss in that span coming in Iowa City in 2017. Kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS with Ohio State (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) set as a 14-point road favorite over Iowa (4-0, 1-0), per DraftKings Sportsbook . College football analyst David Pollack broke down the matchup on his "See Ball Get Ball" podcast. Alabama-Mississippi State, Ohio State-Iowa, Florida-Missouri AND MORE Week 5 CFB Picks https://t.co/8vWS9mTHpm "I think [Iowa] has a chance because Ohio State's defense is more gettable than they've been, but to me that means Iowa has to have some passing game, a little bit of balance, run it more than they've run it, have success and defensively hold the heck on. Like just hold on, don't give up big plays, make them get in the red zone and kick 3s," Pollack said. David Pollack Makes His Pick for Ohio State-Iowa In dissecting the matchup, Pollack focused on two key components. First, he hasn't been impressed by Ohio State's defense, which lost most of its starters from last season, including three of the top 11 picks in the NFL draft. But Pollack also doesn't know how much he trusts Iowa's offense and quarterback Hank Brown to take advantage of that. "I watched every snap of Ohio State vs. Illinois. I thought [the Buckeyes'] defense, I think they've got some guys who flash occasionally, but they gave up over 6 yards a carry to Illinois. To give up almost 200 yards rushing, this is what Iowa is, this is who they want to be -- they want to run the football," Pollack said. "... Hank Brown, he needs to make a few plays down the field. They need to be able to open it up a little bit because I know they're going to run it, and I think they can run it at a decent clip." Iowa ranks 27th nationally in rushing at 215.5 yards per game, led by Kamari Moulton (284 yards and 2 TDs on 7.3 yards per carry) with a few other running backs all contributing in significant ways. But the Hawkeyes rank just 87th in passing at 213.5 YPG while Brown has thrown for 700 yards, 5 TDs and 0 INTs. Iowa's strength, as always, is its defense, which has given up the fewest points in college football (8.0 per game) while ranking 10th at the FBS level overall (239.8 YPG). The Hawkeyes haven't yet played an offense like Ohio State's, however, shutting out Northern Illinois and Northern Iowa while containing limited offenses from Iowa State and Michigan. The Buckeyes are led by two Heisman Trophy candidates in 2025 finalist Julian Sayin (1,206 passing yards, 12 TDs and 1 INT) and star wideout Jeremiah Smith (33 catches for an FBS-leading 617 yards and 7 TDs). In Ohio State's Big Ten opener vs. Illinois last week, a 42-19 win, Smith had 12 catches for 217 yards and 4 TDs. Jeremiah Smith just settled ALL DEBATES, he is the GREATEST WR prospect ever. • 12 receptions (career-high) • 217 receiving yards (career-high) • 4 receiving TD’s (career-high) The Buckeyes WR was UNSTOPPABLE in the GREATEST game of his career 🤯🍿 pic.twitter.com/DhJLDREfJc But Pollack wonders if the Buckeyes' lacking rushing attack (156.75 YPG, 76th nationally) is their vulnerability in a matchup like this. "With Ohio State on the other side, man, is it anybody besides Jeremiah Smith? And here's the thing with Ohio State, can they get that run game going? ... At some point in this season they're going to need to get first downs and punch it in the red zone," Pollack said. As for his ultimate prediction for the matchup, Pollack is taking the Buckeyes and sticking close to the spread set by the oddsmakers. "I think this is a phenomenal matchup. I think Iowa is going to keep it close," he said. "If you weren't watching last week, Illinois kept it close. Illinois was very much in the game until the very last little bit, but they were still very much in striking distance. I think this is 27-13 type of a deal. "I don't think Iowa's offense is good enough. ... It's all about the offense because I think they can hang on long enough, make them kick a few field goals to stay in the game, but the [arrow points toward] Jeremiah Smith and Julian Sayin." IOWA CITY — Starting safety Tyler Brown’s injury status is up in the air for Iowa football’s matchup with Ohio State on Oct. 3. “We’ll see how it looks like,” Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz said Sept. 29. “He’s not fully back. But we’ll see.” There was a concerning sequence involving Brown during the fourth quarter of Iowa’s win over Michigan. Brown was in coverage on a Michigan deep shot. The pass landed incomplete, but Brown came up gingerly. Despite appearing hobbled, Brown stayed in the game. On the very next play, Michigan receiver JJ Buchanan got behind Brown and hauled in a 49-yard touchdown. "The quarterback started scrambling," Brown said. "Everyone knows I’ve been battling through injury, so that’s kind of that.” Asked on Sept. 29 how he is doing health-wise, Brown said: "Good." Brown missed Iowa’s first two games of the season due to a soft-tissue injury. Anthony Hawkins started in Brown’s place. Brown made his Iowa debut against UNI, logging two tackles and forcing a fumble. Brown was Iowa’s fourth-leading tackler against Michigan, tallying nine. But the pair of plays in the fourth quarter were troubling, especially if it caused a health setback. The explosive play gave Michigan the lead and very well could’ve been the deciding score. Fortunately for Iowa, that wasn’t the case as the Hawkeyes put together a 91-yard, touchdown-scoring drive to win the game. On his Always College Football podcast , McElroy picked Florida to win 31-24 on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC. "Florida has a deeper offense," he said, "and Missouri's red zone issues, that's something that's difficult to overcome in this game." Florida jumped from No. 21 to No. 8 in the Top 25 poll after a 52-28 win over No. 4 Ole Miss. picks.blurb: David Pollack Picks Winner of Florida-Missouri Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS A week ago, Florida was the team in prime position to deliver an upset while playing at home against an opponent, Ole Miss, that was coming off a huge win the previous week. The role is reversed in Week 5 for the No. 8-ranked Gators (4-0, 2-0 SEC), who delivered their statement with a 52-28 win over that then-top-5 Rebels team and now must avoid a letdown of their own on the road against No. 25 Missouri (3-1, 0-1). Florida is set as a 5.5-point road favorite, per DraftKings Sportsbook , in a matchup that kicks off at 3:30 p.m. ET Saturday on ABC. College football analyst David Pollack dissected the matchup on his "See Ball Get Ball" podcast. Alabama-Mississippi State, Ohio State-Iowa, Florida-Missouri AND MORE Week 5 CFB Picks https://t.co/8vWS9mTHpm "I want to be Missouri so bad in this matchup because everybody, everybody is like 'Oh, this Buster Faulkner guy's good. This Jon Sumrall guy's good!'" Pollack said of Florida's much ballyhooed new offensive coordinator and head coach. "We've been talking about it for a while -- welcome aboard everybody. "Here's the thing why this matchup becomes really awesome. You have that going for you, again, just like [with Florida vs. Ole Miss] last week, Missouri is playing at home. Florida is not sneaking up on anybody, right?" David Pollack Makes His Prediction For Florida-Missouri Pollack explained why he believes Missouri can potentially be a tough matchup for the Gators and what the Tigers are going to need to do to pull the upset. To put it simply, that requires slowing down running backs Jadan Baugh (600 rushing yards and 11 TDs on 7.2 yards per carry) and Duke Clark (259 yards and 3 TDs on 8.1 YPC) and a Florida rushing attack that ranks 11th nationally at 260.0 YPG while forcing quarterback Aaron Philo to make more plays with his arm. Philo, the Georgia Tech transfer who followed Faulker to Florida and is in his first season as a starter, has only attempted 87 passes in four games for 917 yards, 7 TDs and 2 INTs. Philo was 16-of-23 passing for 196 yards, 1 TD and 0 INTs plus a rushing TD in the win over Ole Miss. "Missouri's defense, watching them vs. Mississippi State, Missouri's defense always finds a way to be physical, they always find a way to be good in the front 7. They can rush the passer, 10 coming off the edge is consistently a problem," Pollack said of edge rusher Daeden Hopkins, who has 6 sacks and 2 forced fumbles already. "... Here's what I'm interested to see, this is the only thing that matters to me, can you put it in Philo's hands? Like literally, at some point who can make Philo be a QB because right now -- and I'm not knocking Philo, they're doing what they need to do and they're undefeated -- but right now Philo is getting worn out by handing that thing off. "Over 300 [rushing yards] a game the last two games against Auburn and Ole Miss. That is a feat, that is impressive. The offensive line is impressive. The system is impressive. Who is going to be the first to say, 'Philo, you've got to beat me'? And can he go through progressions and make those plays when it's not the easy stuff. Can you take away the layups, get him off schedule a little bit? If Missouri can do that at home, that will be interesting for me to watch. That's what I'm looking for the most in this game." Missouri lost its SEC opener 31-24 at Mississippi State last week and has played only one other Power 4 teams so far (a 38-21 win at Kansas). The Tigers are led by quarterback Austin Simmons, the Ole Miss transfer who has passed for 947 yards, 11 TDs and 0 INTs so far. Jamal Roberts (395 rushing yards and 3 TDs on 4.4 YPC) leads the rushing attack, that is still waiting for star Ahmad Hardy to return as he continues to recover and work back from an offseason gunshot wound. Ultimately, Pollack is picking the Gators to win by a comfortable margin. He's a believer in what Sumrall has built in his first season at Florida. "I trust Florida by this point now, I do. I trust them," Pollack said. "I will say this, Florida's receiving corps is banged up to heck. It's going to be very interesting to watch them. I've got Florida 38, Missouri 27ish. I'm trusting Florida on the road after a big game." Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Florida Gators Betting Preview I love first-year Florida head coach John Sumrall, who instantly turned the Gators into a national title contender in his first season in Gainesville. After leading Tulane to the College Football Playoff in 2025, the Gators came knocking with a big contract offer for Sumrall, given how poorly Florida had been for several years under Billy Napier. Florida has been spectacular in just four games under Sumrall. Its offense is averaging over 53 points per game despite facing several difficult SEC foes, including Auburn and Ole Miss . Gators quarterback Aaron Philo has thrown for 917 yards over Florida's first four contests and ranks inside the top 15 in the country with an 85.4 QBR. Florida boasts a loaded offensive unit, primarily led by tailback Jadan Baugh, who has quickly established himself as not just one of the best running backs in college football, but as one of the premier overall players in the nation. Baugh has rushed for an incredible 600 yards over the Gators' first four games and has already found the end zone 11 times, ranking second and first nationally, respectively. Florida's receiving corps has been quite impressive as well. Sophomore wideouts Vernell Brown III and Dallas Wilson have both racked up at least 235 receiving yards on the season. In addition to Sumrall's Gators ranking second in college football with 53.5 points per game, Florida's defense is allowing less than 23 points per game heading into Week 5's SEC showdown. Florida's stop unit has also been under a new regime in 2026, with former Kentucky defensive coordinator Brad White installing multi-faceted three-man and four-man fronts that largely focus on stopping the run, generating pressure, and minimizing explosive plays. While the Gators travel to Austin to play top-ranked Texas in two weeks, Florida will by no stretch of the imagination overlook Saturday's difficult road test against a ranked conference foe in Missouri. Missouri Tigers Betting Preview While Missouri is coming off its first loss of the 2026 season after falling to Mississippi State by a touchdown, the Tigers will be very motivated heading back home to Columbia for a tough Week 5 matchup against the undefeated Gators. Missouri signed head coach Eli Drinkwitz to a six-year contract worth upwards of $10 million annually after the former SEC Coach of the Year led his Tigers to 10 wins in 2023 and again in 2024. Tigers quarterback Austin Simmons has been phenomenal over his first four games as Missouri's QB1 after riding the bench at Ole Miss for two seasons. Simmons has thrown for an impressive 947 yards in the air and 11 touchdowns without throwing a single interception over his first four games in Columbia. Unfortunately for Mizzou's offense, star tailback Ahmad Hardy remains with no timetable for return after ranking second in all of college football with 1,649 rushing yards in 2025. Despite Hardy's absence, the Tigers have still been pretty effective in their rushing attack, with backups Jamal Roberts and Xai'Shaun Edwards carrying the load for Mizzou's backfield in impressive fashion. Missouri boasts an elite receiving corps as well, led by senior wide receiver Cayden Lee , who has already racked up 412 receiving yards to rank ninth in the country. As two former Rebels, Lee and Simmons have quickly re-established their chemistry and have formed a very dangerous connection that has given opposing defenses nightmares. Drinkwitz continues to run a versatile power spread offense using heavy tight end formations to balance short-yardage pounding with perimeter passing, which has led to an uptempo Tiger offense scoring over 35 points per game thus far. Missouri's defensive unit has been quite impressive as well, giving up less than 21 points per game thus far. Senior linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr. has been the anchor for the Tigers' elite front seven. If the Tigers are to pull off the upset in Saturday's SEC clash, it will undoubtedly require a massive effort from this Mizzou defense. We're in for a great matchup on Saturday afternoon between two SEC foes off to promising starts in their respective 2026 campaigns. While I have been very impressed by Missouri's level of play over its first four games, the Tigers must face an uptempo Gators offense that ranks second nationally in points scored this season. Though I definitely expect the Tigers to hang around early, I love Florida in this spot and feel confident backing Sumrall's Gators to cover the 4.5-point spread. Picks: Florida -4.5 (-115)

Florida enters 4-0 and 2-0 in conference play, while Missouri is 3-1 after falling 31-24 at Mississippi State. And right now, the biggest problem for Missouri has a name: Jadan Baugh. away.blurb: Maybe you drank the Kool-Aid. At least for now, you’re forced to spit it out. Maybe you really bought into the hype for a team that was unranked at the start of the year that vaulted into the top 10 after only one really big win. Maybe you chose to ignore the flaws that were there especially in the defensive secondary and maybe when the run game doesn’t do as well as it has, the offense isn’t as good. Whatever the case, this Florida team got a dose of reality when it got waxed at Missouri...now we’ll see how it responds. Look, great coaches have suffered bad losses. Steve Spurrier was blitzed at Tennessee in 1992; Urban Meyer lost 35 to 3 at Alabama his first year on the job. Those guys ended up doing pretty well, don’t you think? But now the question is out there...is this just a one game blip or are there more serious problems with this team than we first thought? First Alert Weather Hurricane HQ Programming Schedule Zeam - News Streams GAINESVILLE, Fla. (WCJB) - If you are a Florida football fan, the sun did come up today. And the loud sound you may have heard was the bubble bursting on the start of the Jon Sumrall era after his team was thoroughly whipped last weekend at Missouri. Remember, at the start of the year most people thought this would be a team that could win seven to nine games and that is certainly very possible. It’s possible they could win more or lose more too. Coach Sumrall was absolutely fuming after the game and he had every right to feel that way but a lot of times we don’t give credit to the other team. Mizzou Coach Eli Drinkwitz has heard all the noise about his program not being able to beat top 25 teams and they were the better and more physical team on this day. And you know that physical part is what is going to drive Sumrall who prides himself on his teams being tough. Lessons are sometimes not learned overnight. But the numbers are alarming. How bad was it? A running back and a quarterback combined for 551 yards in this game. A 300 yard passer and a 200 yard rusher. Injuries didn’t help...Bryce Thornton was a game time scratch and the Gators lost Dijon Johnson during the game, meaning a lot of young and inexperienced players were forced into action in the secondary and it spelled disaster. And who would have thought Missouri would absolutely stone Jaden Baugh and the Florida running game...without it, the offense severely sputtered and you can bet other teams will look to see how they can do the same thing. Although it doesn’t seem that way now, this demoralizing and humiliating game is only one loss and there is still everything ahead for this team to play for. Homecoming against South Carolina is next...we will see how Florida responds. I’m Steve Russell, that’s the Russell Report.

Brown III suffered a knee injury after an 11-yard run in the second quarter during UF's 52-28 win over Ole Miss and did not return. Stockton, meanwhile, suffered a back injury on a helmet-to-helmet targeting hit by Ole Miss safety Joenel Arguero, who was ejected on the play. He returned to field punts in the second half but has been limited in practice this week. If Stockton and Brown are both out, Florida could turn to receivers Eric Singleton Jr., Kahleil Jackson and Micah Mays Jr. for more snaps against Missouri. Singleton returned to the field after sitting out two-plus game with an ankle injury and caught a 38-yard pass against Ole Miss, while also forcing a pass interference penalty. Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy, the SEC's leading rusher from 2025 with 1,649 yards, remains out while recovering from a gunshot wound in his leg. Also out for the Tigers (3-1, 0-1 SEC) are safety, JaDon Blair, running back Malae Fonoti, offensive lineman Josh Atkins and tight end Gavin Hoffman. Edge rushers Langden Kitchen and Darris Smith and linebacker Bobby Washington Jr. are questionable for Missouri. Brown leads the No. 8 Florida Gators (4-0, 2-0 SEC) in receiving with 17 catches for 271 yards and 2 TDs. He's also been a weapon on special teams with two punt returns for TDs. Stockton, meanwhile, has 13 catches for 106 yards and 1 TD on the season. Florida football may need to turn to depth at WR "He played 8-9 snaps," said Florida football offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner, who coached Singleton at Georgia Tech. "He went deep three or four; he got a pass interference; he got the 38-yard gain. So, yeah, he brings a totally different element when it comes to being able to take the top off of defense than really anybody I've ever been around." UF has been relatively healthy so far under first-year coach Jon Sumrall, in part due to a strength and conditioning program under Rusty Whitt that focuses on building strength for injury prevention. Whitt is having players maintain a strict weight room schedule during the regular season. "We've put a lot of work in," Sumrall said. "You know, things that are strong are resilient and don't break easily. So there's a lot of work that's been put in by Rusty (Whitt) and Paul Silvestri and that group. Very grateful for our sports medicine team and strength staff, they all do a phenomenal job." Kevin Brockway is The Gainesville Sun’s Florida beat writer. Contact him at kbrockway@gannett.com. Most everyone is overlooking Florida State, but they can win this game. However, I have far more trust in Tony Elliott to go on the road and get a win to remain unbeaten in ACC play. Xander Tilock: Virginia 38, Florida State 27 At first glance, I was leaning towards picking the Seminoles at home. However, there are two major factors that make it essentially impossible for Florida State to win. The Seminoles have the ACC's second-worst pass defense through four games — so Virginia should have little trouble scoring 35-plus points. However, the other side of the ball is more important, particularly because Florida State has turned the ball over at an average greater than once per game. The Cavaliers can capitalize on those turnovers by turning them into lengthy touchdown drives. Florida State is capable of making things interesting — especially at home — but there are a few reasons why Virginia is the favorite in an ACC road game. This should be a Cavaliers win by multiple scores. Steve DeShazo: Virginia 27, Florida State 31 Saturday brings Virginia's first true road game of 2026. It comes against a proud and talented team that has not played up to its capabilities and may be competing to save Coach Mike Norvell's job in the same way I believe the Cavaliers did for Elliott last year. FSU's offensive skill trio of quarterback Ashton Daniels, receiver Ousman Kromah and receiver Duce Robinson will be a handful for the Cavaliers to contain. Beau Pribula could have a field day passing against the Seminoles, and it may be mandatory to keep Virginia close. The Cavaliers have yet to win a close game or pull out a victory away from home this season. He's playing to a wonderful 11-to-1 touchdown -to-interception ratio, while completing 76.7% of his passes. Do I think those numbers are sustainable? Probably not, but it's still worth mentioning. The one thing that I worry about him, though, is how often he's been sacked. Virginia's offensive line has been a sieve, ranking in the bottom 20 in sack percentage and letting opposing defenses get to its quarterbacks nine total times. And this is a team that primarily likes to run the ball. The Cavaliers are ranked 74th in pass attempts per game, while ranking eighth in rushing attempts. So, yes, there's concern there, because there's nothing spectacular about Virginia's run game. It likes to split the ball between a running back committee because Jekail Middlebrook hasn't separated himself from the pack. Middlebrook hasn't proven to be an effective distance runner, and Xay Davis and Xavier Brown clearly have the efficiency edge. On another note, I really like what the Cavs are doing defensively. They have a deadly secondary led by Jacobie Henderson and Brandyn Hillman. Hillman has already recorded three interceptions and a forced fumble. Not only that, Virginia is one of the best teams in standard down metrics, ranking second in explosiveness allowed and eighth in PPA. Its work against the pass is unsurprisingly its best attribute with Henderson and Hillman, and the Cavs rank fifth in PPA allowed and 10th in success rate allowed. Color me confused on these Seminoles. They're one of the most difficult teams to read in this Group of 6. They started off the season awfully slow against New Mexico State , despite winning, and then got into a slugfest against both SMU and Alabama. And at one point, it seemed like FSU was poised to beat Alabama for the second consecutive season, this time in Tuscaloosa. Quarterback Ashton Daniels seemed like he was lost in the pocket after the first two weeks, played a strong first half against Bama, then threw three interceptions against the Tide. The following week, he threw another pick against Central Arkansas, no less. This is a boom-or-bust team. There's a reason why the Noles have one of the most explosive offenses in the FBS, yet sit 11th in the ACC . Running back Ousmane Kromah has been a star, rushing for 6.4 yards per catch and five touchdowns. Receivers Duce Robinson and Jayvan Boggs are big-time playmakers, but because Daniels is so volatile, they can't be a big part of the offense. Defensively, this is a squad that has some active hands. Currently, 11 players have recorded a pass breakup, including two each from defensive backs Ja'Bril Rawls and Ma'Khi Jones. However, that's all the nice things you'll hear from me about their defense. Florida State ranks near the bottom in nearly every standard down metric. I'm inclined to take Virginia here. Simply, I'm riding with the better team. While this game is being played in Tallahassee, I don't think the Seminoles are good enough defensively to stop the Cavaliers. That's not to say Virginia is perfect, but because Florida State has such a hard time defensively, I see Virginia's offensive line using this game as a "get right" moment. The one concern I have with picking the Cavs is the Daniels factor. He's been known to take off and run. In Virginia's sole loss against West Virginia, the Cavs got chewed up badly by dual-threat quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr., and I can definitely see Daniels using that to his advantage. If Virginia can learn from that loss and not make the same mistakes, this is a prime opportunity to lay the points with the Cavaliers. This is an extremely daunting task, but the only way to eat an elephant is by taking it one bite at a time, and that is exactly what the game will be. Now that the injury reports have gone up for the matchup , it is easier to determine how this game will look. Starting safety Ashlynd Barker has been playing through a broken bone in his arm, although somewhat controversially , to make up for the shocking injury total. The season is on the verge of running off the tracks and the result of this game could smooth things out for another week or completely derail the entire season. Who comes out on top in a battle between former SEC East foes? South Carolina is in the midst of an eight game losing streak to Power Four opponents, which includes seven losses to SEC teams. During this losing streak Beamer's Gamecocks have fallen to Alabama (twice), LSU, Oklahoma, Mississippi State, Texas A&M, and Ole Miss. Their last win came against Kentucky in a 35-13 route of the Wildcats. However now with Will Stein at the helm, this is not the same Kentucky team of recent years. Wildcats QB Kenny Minchey and this offense have been very efficient and moved the ball well. They got a statement win earlier in the year at College Station and are looking for another. What may help South Carolina in this one is Kentucky's leaky defense . The Wildcats rank 14th in scoring (25 ppg), 12th in rushing (122.25 yards per game), and 13th against the pass (234 yards per game). Rain may be in the forecast for this weekend. This very well could play right into the Gamecocks' hands as they have a much improved rushing attack from last season. Kendal Briles should be able to mix up the play calling well and allow LaNorris Sellers to get into a groove. Matt Fuller has topped the 100-yard mark twice in the last three games. The second half was a complete 180, as Kentucky shut out South Alabama and pulled away for a 45-21 victory, and the victory improved Kentucky to 3-1 overall and 1-1 in SEC play. Now, the Wildcats will take on a struggling South Carolina team on the road. The last time Kentucky was on the road, the Wildcats defeated then-No. 9 Texas A&M, 31-21, in College Station. The victory showed how strong Kentucky's defense can be while also giving quarterback Kenny Minchey an opportunity to show what he can become as he continues to develop under first-year head coach Will Stein. South Carolina Gamecocks (2-2, 0-2) The Shane Beamer era is facing increased pressure in Columbia, as South Carolina enters the matchup on a seven-game SEC losing streak. The Gamecocks' last SEC victory came against Kentucky on Sept. 27, 2025, when South Carolina defeated the Wildcats 35-13. South Carolina opened the 2026 season with a dominant 57-0 victory over Kent State, but the Gamecocks have since struggled against SEC competition. South Carolina lost 41-34 at home to Mississippi State before falling to Alabama 49-18 on the road this past weekend. The loss to Alabama dropped the Gamecocks to 0-2 in SEC play. Now, Kentucky comes to Columbia, making this a potentially significant game for Beamer and the Gamecocks. Kentucky is also looking to snap a four-game losing streak against South Carolina. Doing so under Stein would give the Wildcats another significant road victory during his first season. South Carolina will also be without star EDGE Dylan Stewart, who has been suspended indefinitely by Beamer and more than likely will not play against Kentucky. Stewart's suspension came after the Gamecocks' loss to Alabama, during which he threw a punch at Alabama tight end Josh Ford and had a heated interaction with South Carolina's coaching staff. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers remains one of South Carolina's biggest offensive weapons. The dual-threat quarterback opened the season with 270 passing yards and three touchdowns in the Gamecocks' win over Kent State. Wide receiver Nyck Harbor is another player Kentucky will need to account for. Harbor returned to South Carolina for the 2026 season alongside Sellers and remains one of the team's most important receiving threats. Junior running back Matt Fuller is also a name to watch in the South Carolina backfield after showing his ability as both a runner and receiver. South Carolina is on a seven-game SEC losing streak and will be without Stewart, while Kentucky enters the matchup ranked No. 24 in the AP Top 25 and coming off a dominant second half against South Alabama. picks.headline: Kentucky vs. South Carolina prediction: Can Wildcats solve LaNorris Sellers?
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. South Carolina prediction: Can Wildcats solve LaNorris Sellers? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus NFL Power Rankings Rays top sloppy Yankees Week 5 Waiver Wire Falcons run over Saints White Sox up 2-0 in ALDS Kentucky vs. South Carolina prediction: Can Wildcats solve LaNorris Sellers? Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will look to justify its No. 24 ranking at South Carolina on Saturday. The Wildcats are ranked for the first time in almost three years, but if they don't snap a four-game losing streak to the Gamecocks, the stint in The Associated Press Top 25 will not last long. Will Stein's squad has already proven capable of winning in a raucous road environment at Texas A&M, but Stein has been clear he does not believe UK's performance in a win over South Alabama last week was up to the program's standard. Can Kentucky build momentum in advance of a homecoming game against LSU? Can Stein flip the script in a series that has often gone a long way in determining the success of each team's season? Here is what you need to know ahead of the matchup . Kentucky cracked the AP Top 25 for the first time since October 2023 this week but remains in the "others receiving votes" portion of the Coaches Poll. That distinction offers a glimpse at the work the Wildcats still need to do to earn national respect. Upsetting Texas A&M put UK in the spotlight for a week, but now there are real questions about how good the Aggies are. Combine the sluggish opening to the win over South Alabama, and Kentucky's hold on a spot in the Top 25 appears tenuous. "It's cool and all, but I mean that thing shifts every single day," offensive guard Tegra Tshabola said. "We keep focusing on that, we won't be in there long." A win at South Carolina might not move the needle much in terms of national perception since the Gamecocks are 0-2 in SEC play, but it would at least ensure Kentucky remains ranked for its homecoming matchup against LSU next week. Despite UK's spot in the top 25, South Carolina is a three-point favorite as of Friday morning. "I think it's more important for the fans than anything," Stein said. "Our guys got to go play well. I'm not really sure why they rank people this early in the season. There's a lot of games left. It's about playing well on Saturdays. Not letting that dictate how we play. We should play to our standard regardless." Kentucky defensive lineman Kahlil Saunders (92) tries to wrap up South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers (16) during a game at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia, S.C., on Saturday, Sept. 27, 2025. (Ryan C. Hermens/rhermens@herald-leader.com) Another test for UK defense South Carolina was blown out 49-18 at Alabama last week but averaged 45 points per game in its first three games. That stretch included a 41-34 loss to Mississippi State. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers entered the season as a top-50 NFL draft prospect, according to The Athletic, but his performance has been mixed so far. Through four games, Sellers has completed 62.1% of his passes for 833 yards, six touchdowns and four interceptions. He has also rushed for 244 yards and one touchdown on 36 carries. Sellers' stats are boosted by his performance in the season-opening 57-0 win over Kent State in which he completed 19 of 23 passes for 270 yards and three touchdowns. In two SEC games, Sellers has thrown three touchdowns and three interceptions. He also completed just 10 of 23 passes for 96 yards in the Week 2 blowout of Towson but did rush for 119 yards in that game. "I think he's extremely dynamic," Stein said. "He can make every single throw. Big arm, and then when he pulls the ball down, he's very dangerous. They also have really good skill players on offense, so it'll be a big task for our defense to go against these guys, especially in their place." Sellers has given Kentucky fits the last two seasons, completing 21 of 28 passes for 319 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. He rushed for 81 yards on 14 carries last season. Kentucky football injury report Stein downplayed any long-term concerns about UK players who picked up injuries in recent weeks, but the Wildcats will be without at least one key player in Columbia. Junior wide receiver DJ Miller, who was injured while trying to run a deep route against South Alabama, was initially listed as doubtful on the SEC availability report then downgraded to out on Friday. Long snapper Cole Marszalek, backup cornerback Grant Grayton, offensive guards Jay Clark and Aba Selm and linebacker Tavion Wallace were also listed as out Fifth-year linebacker Alex Afari was also listed as unavailable Friday after the Kentucky Court of Appeals dismissed the temporary injunction that had made him and dozens of other athletes eligible in their lawsuit against the NCAA for a fifth season of eligibility. The good news for UK is star defensive tackle Tavion Gadson, who missed the South Alabama game, was not included on the availability report, signalling he is expected to play at South Carolina. Kentucky vs. South Carolina prediction A fast start could be particularly important Saturday with frustrations high among South Carolina fans. If Kentucky can take control of the game early, the atmosphere could grow tense for Shane Beamer and Gamecocks players. A high-scoring affair seems likely, but Kentucky's experience at Texas A&M should help prepare the Wildcats for the moment. Kentucky 35, South Carolina 28. The last word "I don't know a stadium in this league that's not going to be loud. … I would imagine every stadium we go into is going to have crazy fans that are really passionate and make third downs and fourth downs really difficult on the opposing offense. So, it goes back to how do you play good football? Learn how to not beat yourself before you go in. Have to be elite in communication, in operation, in and out of huddles. No huddles, cadence, all that stuff is going to be critical for our success. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alex Joyce Fri, October 2, 2026 at 6:17 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Despite all the troubles from the last two weeks, South Carolina has a chance to get the train back on the track against Kentucky. For a team desparately needing a win, here are three bold predicitions for the Gamecocks that will ultimately end their 2-game skid this season. Usually we try to give you at least one on each side of the ball, however this week we're changing things up. This is an all offense version of bold predictions. We will focus on LaNorris Sellers, the passing game, and the tailbacks. Passing Game looks smooth again It certainly won't be easy. Though Knetucky's "stats" place them in the bottom half of SEC defenses in the passing category, it doesn't tell the full story. In two SEC games the Wildcats held Alabama's Keelon Russell to 188 yards passing and Texas A&M's Marcel Reed to 236 yards. They also lead the conference in interceptions with 6. What gives me confidence in this specific matchup will be South Carolina's ability to run the ball (more on that later). However I believe Seller ends his interception streak this week and keeps this passing game on track. Gamecocks rush for 200+ In their two SEC games this season, Kentucky gave up 155 yards and three touchdowns to Bama. Against Texas A&M they gave up 187 yards and two touchdowns. This is a front seven that can be run on and that's exactly what this Gamecocks' offense does best. Matt Fuller leads a rushing attack that is ranked first in the conference with 262 yards per game. Fuller gained 112 yards on the ground last week as the team put up 216 yards total on Alabama. Against Mississippi State running backs totaled 149 yards. That's good enough for 182.5 yards per game through two contests. Fuller should have his third 100 yard rushing performance of the season which will propel the Gamecocks to a win. picks.blurb: Kentucky Looks To End Its South Carolina Losing Streak; Preview & Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus NFL Power Rankings Rays top sloppy Yankees Week 5 Waiver Wire Falcons run over Saints White Sox up 2-0 in ALDS Kentucky Looks To End Its South Carolina Losing Streak; Preview & Prediction | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Tony Siracusa, CFB Managing Editor Kevin McGuffey Thu, October 1, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It wasn't the prettiest game last Saturday as Kentucky broke open a close game to pull away from South Alabama in the second half. As a result, Will Stein's club now sits at 3-1, which is the best record at this point in the season since 2023. In addition, they find themselves ranked number 24 in this week's coaches poll. On Saturday, they hit the road for the second time this season, looking for a similar result as the trip to Texas A&M. To do that, they'll have to beat a team they've had little recent success against. Furthermore, they'll face a club whose coach is not only firmly on the hot seat, but some think could be coaching for his job. Let's look at both clubs, give you some series history and a prediction as Kentucky looks to end a South Carolina losing streak. Kentucky Looks To End Its South Carolina Losing Streak Looking At The Positives To say Stein wasn't happy after last Saturday's win over the Jaguars would be an understatement. After the game, the UK head man said, "If you think for one second this is the way you play football at Kentucky, it's going to be a long season." Even with that, some good things happened. Kentucky had three running backs, CJ Baxter, Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes, all run for over 100 yards. It's the first time that's happened since a game with Ole Miss in 2020. As a result, the Big Blue Wall continues to get accolades from around the nation. Another positive for the Cats has been the play of quarterback Kenny Minchey. After finally getting to be a starter, Minchey has completed 69 percent of his passes for 876 yards and eight touchdowns on only one interception. Even better for Kentucky fans, he played his best game so far in the win over Texas A&M on the road. He'll need to be that good again on Saturday. Speaking of the opponent, let's take a look as Kentucky looks to end a South Carolina losing streak. Scouting The Gamecocks Shane Beamer's squad comes into Saturday sporting a 2-2 record but 0-2 in conference play. In addition, they've given up 90 points in the two league losses. The two victories came over Kent State and Towson, while they lost to Mississippi State and Alabama. The offense is led by quarterback LaNorris Sellers. Through four games, he's completed 62 percent of his passes for 833 yards and six touchdowns. However, he does have four interceptions. Furthermore, he's a threat running the ball with 284 yards and a touchdown. His favorite target has been running back Matthew Fuller. Not only does he lead the team with 13 receptions, but he's also the top runner with 384 yards. Right behind Fuller is the combination of Nyck Harbor and Mazeo Bennett Jr., who have 21 catches for 278 yards and a couple of scores. The passing game has been an issue this year as Sellers has only four completions of over 20 yards. For them to have a chance against a good Kentucky secondary, they'll need more production than that. On the defensive side of the ball, one player Kentucky won't have to worry about is defensive end Dylan Stewart. He was suspended for this week's game after punching an Alabama player and having a heated exchange on the Carolina sideline. He's made a career out of tormenting the Wildcats, and his not being in the lineup is a definite plus for the Cats. Linebacker Justin Okoronkwo leads the defense with 26 tackles while defensive lineman Anthony Addison leads with three sacks. Overall, they are one of the worst in the country at giving up big plays. That's something that could play in the Wildcats' favor. Now that we've looked at both teams, let's look at the long rivalry between the two schools as Kentucky looks to end a South Carolina losing streak. Photo courtesy: David Leong-Imagn Images Series History Saturday's game marks the 37th time in history the Cats and Gamecocks have met. Currently, South Carolina leads the series 22 wins to 13 with one tie. The first meeting came back in 1937, which UK won 27-7. Since USC joined the SEC in 1992, they've played every year. In fact, the two will play each other through 2029 as permanent opponents. Over the years, this series has been one of streaks. First, the Gamecocks won 10 straight from 2000-2009 before UK broke through in 2010. Kentucky flipped the script, winning seven of eight from 2014-2021. Since then, it's gone back the other way with USC winning the last four. There's only one thing left in our preview, and that's a prediction as Kentucky looks to end a South Carolina losing streak. Who Wins On Saturday? Whenever the Cats and Gamecocks meet, it always seems that the victor uses the win as a springboard to a good season. For Kentucky, a win will only enhance their bowl prospects. On the other side of the ball, Beamer needs this one badly. His seat couldn't get much hotter than it is now, unless they lose on Saturday. After making the Citrus Bowl in 2024, the program has fallen off. In fact, they've only won one game against a power conference team over the last two years. That team, you guessed it, Kentucky. Beamer and former UK coach Mark Stoops sparred back and forth over the last few years. In a bit of irony, some have compared what's going on in Columbia to Stoops' last two years in Lexington. Look for USC to pull out all the stops to get the win, and we'll set the over/under on "Sandstorm" at 50. In the end, Kentucky's the better team, and they get the win, and Beamer's seat gets even hotter. away.blurb: It's a knee injury for Morton, who apparently hurt it during a recent practice. He is set to be out indefinitely, and will be re-evaluated in a few weeks. Unfortunately, it appears that this one will have him out for a while, including into the regular season. Morton transferred to Kentucky this offseason from Washington State, but was born in the Bluegrass State. He is a very good three-point shooter, and had a terrific summer with Pope and the Cats. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings ACC frontrunner and No. 4 Miami travels to Death Valley for a Saturday night clash at Clemson Getty Images The race for the ACC title heads to a familiar location when No. 4 Miami visits Death Valley to take on Clemson on Saturday. The Tigers, despite a 16-8 record against AP-ranked opponents at home under Dabo Swinney, find themselves as heavy underdogs to Mario Cristobal's Hurricanes, and hope to use this stage to reaffirm their place as an ACC contender. Miami and Clemson are the only two teams with a 2-0 record in ACC play, so this makes Saturday's game a battle for solo first place in the standings. That's exactly where Miami expected to be as a top-five team with national title aspirations, but it's also been an elusive goal during 22 years of conference membership. While Miami has had great seasons since joining the league in 2004, including reaching the national championship game last season, it has yet to win the ACC Championship in football and has only played in the title game once. The opponent in that one ACC Championship Game was against Dabo Swinney and Clemson in 2017, with the Hurricanes being the third of six consecutive teams to lose to the Tigers in Charlotte. The all-time series between these two national title-winning programs is split dead even at 7-7, with each team winning half of their games at home (8 at Miami, 4 at Clemson) and each team winning one of the two neutral-site meetings. Miami vs. Clemson: Need to know Darian Mensah is building a Heisman Trophy case : This game will be a big-time stage for Miami quarterback Darian Mensah and any prospects he or other teammates could have for award recognition at the end of the year. Even as the oddsmakers have identified little difference between Miami playing Clemson and another ACC opponent like Pittsburgh or Virginia Tech , a more mainstream view would target the Tigers as Miami's biggest foe in the conference, making this Saturday night primetime stage an opportunity for Mensah to prove his candidacy against top competition. Through four games, Mensah has been the runaway leader for best quarterback in the country, completing 88.7% of his passes at 11.4 yards per attempt with 14 touchdowns and zero interceptions. Clemson might be struggling offensively at the moment, but its defense, particularly against the pass, has been leading the way the last couple of weeks. It's a worthy opponent for Mensah to make his case as the most outstanding player in college football , and the national audience will be dialed in to put that claim to the test. Miami has been historically dominant : The Hurricanes are not just 4-0 overall and 2-0 in the ACC; they have been beating teams by historic margins and have hinted at the potential to be one of this season's true juggernauts. Miami has been beating its opponents by an average of 42.8 points per game, which is the most in school history through four games. The closest margin came in a 13-point road win at Wake Forest last week, and the Demon Deacons' subsequent win at Louisville further highlights the value of that victory. Miami has jumped all over opponents early in games, holding three of its four foes to under 100 yards of offense in the first half and scoring fast and early behind the firepower that comes from Mensah, Malachi Toney and the rest of an offense that's averaging 51.8 points per game. Dabo Swinney is one win away from tying an ACC legend: Clemson coach Dabo Swinney is one win away from tying Florida State legend Bobby Bowden for the most head coaching wins in ACC regular season play (117). Swinney already holds the conference record for overall wins as an ACC head coach thanks to the Tigers' success in postseason games, but it does provide an interesting wrinkle as Dabo stares down a potential statement game against Miami. Swinney and the state of his program have been under fire since a disastrous 51-10 loss to LSU in the season, but the 3-0 response since has hinted at a level of resiliency that can help the team remain competitive. If Clemson were to find a way to pull off the upset so Dabo matches Bowden for the regular-season ACC wins record, it would be a heat check for ACC's new-money power and also one of the legend's fiercest rivals. Where to watch Miami vs. Clemson live Date : Saturday, Oct. 3 | Time : 7:30 p.m. ET Location : Memorial Stadium -- Clemson, South Carolina TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Miami vs. Clemson prediction, picks While Dabo Swinney gets skewered for his lack of transfer portal activity compared to his peers, it should be noted that key pieces of an improving pass defense have come via transfer pickups. Clemson has allowed fewer than 150 passing yards in each of the past two games, including an impressive showing against talented California quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele . I think that group can hold the Hurricanes in check just enough to keep this game lower scoring than the total suggests. Miami @ Clemson Preview And Prediction
picks.blurb: Miami @ Clemson Preview And Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus NFL Power Rankings Rays top sloppy Yankees Week 5 Waiver Wire Falcons run over Saints White Sox up 2-0 in ALDS Miami @ Clemson Preview And Prediction Sep 26, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah (10) looks on from the field against the Central Michigan Chippewas during the third quarter at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, September 29, 2026 at 5:22 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One of the biggest ACC games of the season takes place Saturday night as No. 4 Miami heads to Death Valley to take on Clemson . Miami enters 4-0 and 2-0 in the ACC, while Clemson sits at 3-1 and 2-0 in conference play. The Tigers have won three straight since getting embarrassed 51-10 by LSU in the opener, including a 24-10 road win over Cal last week. But Clemson hasn't faced anything quite like this Miami team since that LSU disaster. The Hurricanes are averaging 51.8 points and 588.8 yards per game , ranking first nationally in total offense. Even scarier, Miami's defense is allowing only 9.0 points and 224.5 yards per game . How Miami Wins It starts with Darian Mensah . Mensah has been ridiculously efficient this season. He completed 23 of 27 passes for 338 yards and three touchdowns in Miami's 52-3 win over Central Michigan, pushing his season completion percentage to an absurd 88.7% . Miami needs to let Mensah attack Clemson early and take the crowd out of the game. Malachi Toney gives him an elite weapon on the outside, while the Hurricanes have enough balance on the ground to prevent Clemson from simply sitting back against the pass. Defensively, the formula is simple: make Clemson throw the football. The Tigers are averaging only 156.3 passing yards per game, while Miami enters with the nation's No. 1 rushing defense at just 39.5 yards allowed per game. If Miami shuts down Clemson's rushing attack early, this matchup could become extremely uncomfortable for the Tigers. How Clemson Wins Clemson needs Death Valley to become a factor immediately. The Tigers cannot afford to get into a shootout with Miami. They need long possessions, a strong rushing performance from Gideon Davidson and at least a couple of turnovers from their defense. Davidson is coming off 159 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Cal , and Clemson will likely need another big performance from him to keep Mensah standing on the sideline. If Clemson falls behind by multiple scores and is forced to throw its way back into the game, Miami has a massive advantage. I think Clemson makes this interesting early. It's a Saturday night game in Death Valley, Clemson has won three straight and the Tigers' defense has shown significant improvement since that LSU embarrassment. But Miami is simply playing at a different level right now. Mensah eventually starts finding holes in the Clemson defense, Miami takes away the Tigers' running game and the Hurricanes begin pulling away in the second half. Clemson has improved, but Miami looks like a legitimate College Football Playoff and national championship contender.
