(Patrick Breen/The Republic) 1 / 29 Tait Reynolds, Clemson football freshman quarterback for Dabo Swinney Tait Reynolds, Clemson football freshman quarterback for Dabo Swinney How much of this game will have to be decided by Reynolds, who is a freshman? This is one heck of a spotlight for just his third start. The Tigers have done their best to alleviate pressure on him with their run game, but Miami leads the ACC with 39.5 rushing yards allowed per game. Clemson may give Gideon Davidson carry after carry, but there will be a time when the Tigers need some big passing plays. Reynolds doesn't have to be Superman, but he has to show some growth. Can he? The combination of a still-developing freshman and an offensive line that's been so-so in pass protection plays into Miami's hands, especially with how much pressure the Hurricanes have been getting on quarterbacks. Clemson is still figuring things out with Reynolds, while Miami has a quarterback with no questions. Darian Mensah will look to do what he did last season at Duke and pick Clemson apart. The Tigers have a strong secondary, but it'll be their toughest challenge yet. Even if Mensah has an off day, the Hurricanes have a strong rushing attack that's gained over 120 yards in all four games. Miami is most likely to have a balanced offense, and it also doesn't have a clear weakness on defense. Clemson's rushing defense struggled against LSU and North Carolina, and while it did better against California, the Golden Bears are averaging an ACC-worst 101.5 rushing yards per game. Clemson vs. Miami scouting report Where Clemson has an advantage: Miami hasn't faced a secondary as good as Clemson's. Ashton Hampton leads the ACC with five pass breakups, and Elliot Washington II is tied for second with three interceptions. Getting Corian Gipson back at nickel would only strengthen an already sound unit. Clemson's secondary will have its hands full though. Mensah has been the nation's most efficient and accurate quarterbacks. But the Tigers are well-equipped to meet the challenge, just like they did against Cal's Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele . Where Miami has an advantage: The Hurricanes look better at the line of scrimmage. Miami ranks second in the ACC with 227.5 rushing yards per game, and running backs Javian Mallory and Mark Fletcher Jr. are averaging 9 and 6.5 yards per carry, respectively. Miami also looks better on the other side. Marquise Lightfoot is tied for fourth in the ACC with four sacks, while Damon Wilson II and Armondo Blount can win one-on-one. Miami generated pressure on 60.8% of Wake Forest's dropbacks in its last ACC game, and Reynolds is 20 of 46 for 175 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions when he's under pressure or blitzed. The Hurricanes might be better than LSU. They have arguably the nation's best quarterback, one of the nation's most electric wide receivers and a dominant defense. Miami is better in too many areas. picks.blurb: Miami vs Clemson recap: Hurricanes take down Tigers, 41-13 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus NFL Power Rankings Rays top sloppy Yankees Week 5 Waiver Wire Falcons run over Saints White Sox up 2-0 in ALDS Miami vs Clemson recap: Hurricanes take down Tigers, 41-13 Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The banged-up Miami Hurricanes added more injuries to their list, but they outlasted Clemson 41-13 in a key night game in Death Valley that sends them into their bye week feeling like a legitimate national championship contender once again. No. 4 Miami (5-0, 3-0 in ACC) passed its first big test, though maybe not quite with flying colors. Yes, the offense remained explosive with Darian Mensah accounting for two very impressive touchdowns. The second play of the game was a screen that Cooper Barkate took 61 yards for a score . Then the QB ran in a 34-yard TD on a thrilling scramble up the middle and hopped on his own fumble in the end zone. And yes, the defensive front looked absolutely terrifying once again, with Damon Wilson II putting up 2.5 sacks as part of a six-sack effort against freshman QB Tait Reynolds. Gideon Davidson and the talented running backs of the Tigers (3-2, 2-1) were held to 0 net yards in the first half and 55 yards overall, though Davidson did score the first rushing touchdown of the year on the Hurricanes D. Watch Miami vs Clemson game live on Fubo (free trial) But there are legitimate concerns, none more so than the building pile of injuries. Right guard Max Buchanan and tackle Matthew McCoy both went down in the second quarter , though both did return in the third. The same could not be said for Marquise Lightfoot , Miami's tackles and sacks leader who left in the second quarter and did not return. With the ongoing injuries to the secondary, the Canes can't afford many more injuries to one of the top defense in the nation if it wants to get back to the College Football Playoff. Clemson also was in the game longer than expected. Six straight drives all ended at least at midfield, with two in a row ending inside the red zone. The drives went punt, field goal, punt, punt, field goal, turnover on downs. T.J. Brown and Bryant Wesco Jr. had impressive days against the Miami secondary, which desperately needs O.J. away.blurb: "I think our guys do a really good job being able to take, like, minor adjustments or little details, and as a staff, I think our guys do a really good job of helping out, hey, this is where maybe we got to clean something up, or maybe a better call in this situation might be this, and, you know, being able to react and respond, and then also understanding, like, hey, the play off of this is probably going to be this shot or this moving pocket or this a run that’s a little bit different where the scheme might fit a little bit different, a tweak here or there, and our guys can handle that pretty well," Hetherman said. "And I just think that’s our guys putting in the effort during the week, putting in the effort in the offseason to understand what’s happening when I’m blocking man away, blocking when I’m getting certain pictures in the box or out of the box, and understanding the game of football." After the Canes and Hetherman figure out what they like to do and lock them down. Some teams struggle to get past the 50-yard line, while Miami has its team ready to pin its back to attack and get after the quarterback. Miami's sack total might only be 10, but they are one of the best teams in the country at quarterback pressure. If the ball is not out within 2.5 seconds, other teams are at the mercy of the Hurricanes. CORAL GABLES, Fla. — Last season, the Miami Hurricanes spent time inside the top 10 of overall defense with the best pass-rushing duo in the country along with some of the best corner play in the country. Statistically , No. 4 Miami is better this season. Over four weeks, the Hurricanes rank as the No. 2 overall defense in the land, only behind No. 3 Notre Dame . They are the No. 4-ranked scoring defense but still have some areas to clean up, with sacks and turnovers starting to increase. But how is this possible with the Hurricanes missing their top two cornerbacks and best young linebackers on the roster? It's simple: defensive coordinator Corey Hetherman . Schemes and defensive adjustments are the calling card for Hetherman and this Hurricanes defense. The first drive of each Miami game, depending on the talent of the opposing offense, will likely get the first drive down the field and add some points to the board. The process is simple for Hetherman, and the defense changes. Learn, adjust, and adapt. It doesn't have to wait until the second half if something can be fixed quickly. Most times, those quick fixes are all it takes for the Hurricanes to get roaring. Moreover, with that mindset, the Hurricanes have only allowed four offensive touchdowns this season. One to start the season against Stanford, and the rest came against Wake Forest, who are better than most give them credit for. Miami's offense will get most of the praise as it should. away.headline: ACC football power rankings week 6: Chaos, cruel injuries, and the red-hot race behind Miami
away.blurb: Five weeks into the college football season, the Atlantic Coast Conference has officially entered a state of beautiful, unpredictable madness. If you thought you were starting to figure out the conference, Week 5 blew those assumptions out of the water. From statement blowouts in legendary stadiums to a devastating injury that alters a dark-horse championship run, the hierarchy is morphing by the minute. Manny Diaz’s squad enjoyed a restful bye week and watched the teams around them deal with chaos. Armed with an elite defense that has surrendered just 44 points all season, the undefeated Duke Blue Devils hold a premium spot in the ACC football power rankings. They return to action this weekend in a high-stakes road game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets . The SMU Mustangs navigated a literal and figurative storm, grinding out a 25-16 win over the Boston College Eagles in torrential downpours. They have physical depth, but they will need to discover an extra gear through the air to stay in the title conversation. Despite jumping out to a 14-0 lead on Pitt, Virginia Tech could not hold off a furious rally by the Panthers, as the Hokies fell 35-33. Virginia Tech has the athleticism to compete with anyone, but self-inflicted mistakes are preventing a true breakthrough. Head coach Dabo Swinney insisted post-game that his team is “right there”, but the film tells a different story. Getting embarrassed on your home turf by Miami exposed a massive bridge to cross if Clemson wants to find itself back in national relevance. They are well out of the top-five in this week’s ACC football power rankings, but the schedule softens for Clemson considerably from here on out, so it’ll be interesting to see if they can take advantage of it. As we go further into October, predicting who will join the conference elite in Charlotte is an exercise in volatility. This definitive look at the top 10 of the ACC football power rankings dissects the contenders, the pretenders, and the teams desperately looking for answers. ACC Football Power Rankings Week 6 1. Miami Hurricanes (5-0, 3-0 ACC) There is no debate at the top of the ACC football power rankings. The Miami Hurricanes went into Death Valley and completely dismantled the Clemson Tigers in a 41-13 blowout victory. Darian Mensah operated the offense with surgical precision, while the defensive line completely suffocated the Tigers. Entering their bye week, Miami looks entirely unrivaled with Mensah leading the way . It is their conference to lose. 2. Duke Blue Devils (4-0, 1-0 ACC) 3. Pittsburgh Panthers (5-0, 2-0 ACC) The Pittsburgh Panthers proved their mettle with a gutsy, dramatic 35-33 road victory at Lane Stadium against the Virginia Tech Hokies. away.blurb: The Miami football team has been battling injuries all season. But there's been good news coming out of Coral Gables leading up to a prime-time ACC test at Clemson . The final injury report revealed which Hurricanes will be back tonight. Fletcher, who led the ACC with 1,192 rushing yards with 14 total touchdowns in 2025 and leads the Hurricanes with 230 yards this year, sustained an upper-body injury that forced him to miss most of the fourth quarter in a tighter-than-expected victory against Wake. His health became even more important when No. 2 back Marty Brown was ruled out for the rest of the season after a knee injury earlier in the game. With Moten already out, Miami's other starting defensive tackle, Armondo Blount, got banged up vs. CMU. It was the latest in a string of injuries affecting the Canes' defense, down its two starting cornerbacks — O.J. Frederique and Xavier Lucas — since Week 1. Key backups Ja'Boree Antoine and Damari Brown have also been out, but despite the injuries, UM still fields the No. 2 defense in the nation by yards, No. 4 in points and No. 1 in rush yards. The following players have been ruled out according to Saturday's final injury report: WR Joshua Moore (out for season), RB CharMar Brown (out for season), DB Xavier Lucas, DB Ja'Boree Antoine, DB O.J. Frederique, TE Owen Ruskavich, TE Luka Gilbert (out for season). Lucas moved from questionable to out on Friday night. After sitting out last week's game against Central Michigan, running back Mark Fletcher was not on the injury report ahead of today's game at Clemson, signifying he is likely to play. If he is unavailable, Miami will split carries between Javian Mallory, Girard Pringle Jr. and Jordan Lyle with Chris Wheatley-Humphrey sprinked in. Clemson would lean its defense more on containing Malachi Toney and the passing game. Coach Mario Cristobal said running back Mark Fletcher and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten were held out against Central Michigan for precautionary reasons and that both were "ready to roll." Asked about the slew of defenders who missed or were injured during the CMU game, Cristobal said Sept. 28 that the biggest playmakers — Moten and fellow defensive tackle Armondo Blount — were good to go against Clemson. He also said cornerback Xavier Lucas, who was injured in the opener at Stanford and hasn't played since, could be back tonight, but his status changed from questionable to out Friday night. away.headline: Miami football injury struggles open new opportunities
away.blurb: Week three’s road trip to Wake Forest decimated Miami’s health, losing backup running back Marty Brown (knee) and WR3 Joshua Moore (upper-body) for the season. Crucial starters in Ahmad Moten Sr., WR Malachi Toney, and RB Mark Fletcher all got banged up to a more limited extent. The position group most heavily impacted by injuries is the secondary with Frederique, Lucas, Ja’Boree Antoine out for extended periods with Damari Brown nicked up as well. While sophomore safety Bryce Fitzgerald theoretically plugs in well at corner due to his length and athleticism, it has been glaringly obvious that he is playing out of position so far this season. Fitzgerald referred to him as a “freak of nature” after his first four games, indicating that his expanded role is not likely to diminish even when the guys in front of him return. Sophomore wideout Malachi Toney is on pace for 102 catches, 1,700+ yards, and 18 touchdowns following his record-breaking freshman season. However, despite this elite production from the Heisman candidates, the offense has lost multiple weapons with Brown and Moore out for the season. The Hurricanes are lucky to have the two best statistical receivers in the country from a year ago in the same room, and need to maximize their talent. The same could not be said for Marquise Lightfoot , Miami's tackles and sacks leader who left in the second quarter and did not return. With the ongoing injuries to the secondary, the Canes can't afford many more injuries to one of the top defense in the nation if it wants to get back to the College Football Playoff. Clemson also was in the game longer than expected. Six straight drives all ended at least at midfield, with two in a row ending inside the red zone. The drives went punt, field goal, punt, punt, field goal, turnover on downs. T.J. Brown and Bryant Wesco Jr. had impressive days against the Miami secondary, which desperately needs O.J. Frederique and Xavier Lucas to return. On Clemson's first play after Mark Fletcher's touchdown, Damon Wilson II forced Tait Reynolds out of the pocket to the left. He tried to scramble, but Herbert Scroggins III wrapped up his ankles and Ahmad Moten came from behind to deliver a powerful punch to the ball. Scroggins fell on it, and after an official review, the fumble recovery was upheld. The Hurricanes take over at the Tigers' 27. Clemson has been driving consistently, but once again, when they got near scoring range, the Miami pass rush halted their efforts. This time, Ahmad Moten led the way up the gut and teamed up with Damon Wilson for a big third-down sack. Now back at the 46-yard line, Clemson had no choice but to punt. Like running back Mark Fletcher, Moten was held out of last week's game against Central Michigan after a shoulder injury at Wake Forest . As trainers were tending to guard Max Buchanan, ABC sideline reporter Holly Rowe said cornerback Ethan O'Connor went back to the locker room with an injury. The Hurricanes are reeling with injuries in the secondary, as starting corners O.J. Frederique and Xavier Lucas have been out since getting injured in the opener. O'Connor has one of the Canes' two interceptions this year. On a Javian Mallory 4-yard run, guard Max Buchanan stayed on the field with an injury. Trainers came out and were working on his right leg. He was helped up and walked off the field with assistance. Mark Fletcher's first run of the game went up the gut for 6 yards, his first carry since the fourth quarter against Wake Forest on Sept. 18. He then took a swing pass 5 yards for a first down, then took a handoff 4 yards off the left side. The senior's return is a welcome one, especially after No. 2 back Marty Brown was lost for the season at Wake. home.headline: With another Clemson player out for season, bye week ‘coming at a good time’ for Tigers
home.blurb: Clemson football is down another player for the season as the Tigers’ bye week comes at a good time, according to coach Dabo Swinney. The team will return to play Charleston Southern on Oct. 17. Top Story With another Clemson player out for season, bye week ‘coming at a good time’ for Tigers By Jackson Castellano jcastellano@postandcourier.com Jackson Castellano “I think most coaches would like a bye week somewhere close to the middle,” coach Dabo Swinney said. “So that's worked out for us. I think it's coming at a good time.” Swinney also pointed out that Clemson’s opponent out of the bye could be helpful for his team. He couldn’t recall the last time the Tigers played a non-power conference opponent coming off a break because they never have in the Swinney era. Swinney’s team is in some phase of recovery at nearly every position. The most pressing update to the injury report is defensive back Corian Gipson. Swinney announced at his off-week teleconference on Oct. 5 that Clemson’s starting nickel needs season-ending surgery. Gipson left the North Carolina game Sept. 19 early with an injury and didn’t play the following week at Cal. He did play against Miami , and an MRI after the game determined Gipson required a meniscus procedure. Ronan Hanafin and Donovan Starr are likely to see more reps at nickel in Gipson’s absence, per Swinney. Ashton Hampton might also get some work in the slot, in which case Branden Strozier would take his place on the outside. Gipson is the fourth Clemson player to go down for the year in 2026. Freshman safety Polo Anderson tore his ACL in preseason. Defensive tackle Markus Strong and running back David Eziomume had similar season-ending leg injuries. Running back Jarvis Green will miss Clemson’s next game as he recovers from an injury. Jay Haynes, who missed the Miami game due to a funeral, will be key in the Tigers’ current backfield rotation of Gideon Davidson, Chris Johnson Jr. and Haynes with Green and Eziomume sidelined. home.headline: Miami injury report: Is Mark Fletcher playing vs Clemson?
home.blurb: The Miami football team has been battling injuries all season. But there's been good news coming out of Coral Gables leading up to a prime-time ACC test at Clemson . The final injury report revealed which Hurricanes will be back tonight. Fletcher, who led the ACC with 1,192 rushing yards with 14 total touchdowns in 2025 and leads the Hurricanes with 230 yards this year, sustained an upper-body injury that forced him to miss most of the fourth quarter in a tighter-than-expected victory against Wake. His health became even more important when No. 2 back Marty Brown was ruled out for the rest of the season after a knee injury earlier in the game. With Moten already out, Miami's other starting defensive tackle, Armondo Blount, got banged up vs. CMU. It was the latest in a string of injuries affecting the Canes' defense, down its two starting cornerbacks — O.J. Frederique and Xavier Lucas — since Week 1. Key backups Ja'Boree Antoine and Damari Brown have also been out, but despite the injuries, UM still fields the No. 2 defense in the nation by yards, No. 4 in points and No. 1 in rush yards. The following players have been ruled out according to Saturday's final injury report: WR Joshua Moore (out for season), RB CharMar Brown (out for season), DB Xavier Lucas, DB Ja'Boree Antoine, DB O.J. Frederique, TE Owen Ruskavich, TE Luka Gilbert (out for season). Lucas moved from questionable to out on Friday night. After sitting out last week's game against Central Michigan, running back Mark Fletcher was not on the injury report ahead of today's game at Clemson, signifying he is likely to play. If he is unavailable, Miami will split carries between Javian Mallory, Girard Pringle Jr. and Jordan Lyle with Chris Wheatley-Humphrey sprinked in. Clemson would lean its defense more on containing Malachi Toney and the passing game. Coach Mario Cristobal said running back Mark Fletcher and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten were held out against Central Michigan for precautionary reasons and that both were "ready to roll." Asked about the slew of defenders who missed or were injured during the CMU game, Cristobal said Sept. 28 that the biggest playmakers — Moten and fellow defensive tackle Armondo Blount — were good to go against Clemson. He also said cornerback Xavier Lucas, who was injured in the opener at Stanford and hasn't played since, could be back tonight, but his status changed from questionable to out Friday night. home.blurb: The first injury report is out ahead of No. 4 Miami hitting the road to take on Clemson in Death Valley . The Hurricanes have been battling injuries all season , and in the last game against Central Michigan, many key starters were out for safety, giving others a chance to shine in their moment. However, some continued to pop up on the injury report, and now, with the return to ACC play, the Hurricanes have to report an injury list, allowing a glimpse into what has been happening behind the scenes. The Hurricanes best conerback has been moved from out to questionable alining with what the head coach Mario Cristobal said in his update about the star player. Ethan O'Connor has been elite to start the season, being graded as the highest-rated cornerback in the country. The addition of Lucas beside him not only gives a boost to the Canes' defense by moving others back into their true position, but it also gives the Canes more turnover threats all over the field.
